The claim was on main before the first spawn; the open partial claim of cleanup wave 05 (2026-10-21T1147Z-audit, wave=05, older than 48 h) was ignored under Phase 0 step 2. Monthly calibration: not due (the 2026-11-01 report owns November). ATT&CK pin: up to date, local v20.1 equals upstream v20.1.

  • Truth passes: 49 entries in scope (34 new, 15 updated), 1,426 claims, all answered: 24 clean, 22 imprecision, 3 factual-error (Drupal SA-CORE-2026-017 exploitation unrecorded, Oracle CSPU "none exploited", ScreenConnect August link). Out of scope under v4.22: 22 entries carrying only 2026-11-15 audit records plus its recovered ARTEX-in-AWS entry.
  • Records: 25 entries carry one record each from this fire (7 update, 9 correction, 9 improvement; 5 internal), including the out-of-scope Brotli entry, whose Mitel advisory moved to revision 6.0 (a pre-pass lead).
  • Recovered entries (2): Synology-SA-26:21 (CVE-2026-120382) and Huntress's timeroasting detection research. The Unit 42 Com-vishing report is correctly droppable; the 2026-11-21 fire's call stands.
  • Declined findings: Cisco Secure Email Gateway critical kept and its Metasploit record left typed as improvement (append-only); Puppet kept at notable; Java4Shell record-summary count (append-only); Turla DLL names (hijacked legitimate names, not indicators); EUVD API citations; HPE sourcing-note timestamp. Reasons in the report.
  • Contradiction: the LiteLLM chain entry records GTIG's description of the exploited CVE-2026-40217 as a key-regeneration rebind against the vendor's sandbox-escape description; no source reconciles them.
  • Pre-pass leads decided by the main agent: the two Publica NZZ quotes are unverifiable on a paywalled teaser (watch item); the Mitel lead was a revision (recorded); php2shell (Trend status table revised 2026-11-18) and agent-framework (SafeDep removed the sentence on 2026-11-18) were decided by TB and TD as page revisions.
  • Calibration alarm: in-scope high is 15 of 49 after this audit (Drupal added); all 14 earlier high entries were re-graded against the Phase 4 bar and clear it.
  • KEV: nine additions in the window, all covered (kev-window.txt); no COVERED-STALE or RANSOMWARE row. Backlog: no open row.
  • Rotational lookback: one sweep defect (Synology listing, fixed by the 2026-11-22 fire's recipe), one rotation lag (Huntress, unswept 2026-11-15 to 11-22).
  • Fix effectiveness (2026-11-15): v4.25's slice-only attempt rule held (25 outside-slice checks, none counted); the entry-shape uncited-source check passes over the window.
  • Warning sweep: Phase 0 check_run.py --all 1 warn · 0 fail · 29 acknowledged; one acknowledgment added (2026-11-19T0355Z-intel single CLEAN at the cap), none removed; site/build.py emits no self-check warning.
  • Source health: the one UNSOLVED source, checkpoint-support, reads relevant on its existing recipe (transient block); safeonweb-be recovered. Reader pool: every key exhausted (context only).
  • Session budget: 14 of 20 spawns (6 truth passes, 3 re-sweeps, 5 verifier iterations, no follow-up research), 6,982,947 sub-agent tokens (work/2026-11-22T1407Z-audit/budget.tsv). No secondary work ran.
  • Verification: five iterations, all NEEDS_FIXES; truth plus editorial fell 15, 7, 6, 3, 2. Iteration 5 met the low-residual early exit (truth 1, editorial 1, no F1 or F4); its two remediations (the Fortinet FortiClient citation split, Integrated PA Suite Tester in the Brotli Exposure line) were applied after the pass, so the residual recorded is 2.
  • Coverage gaps: lab52 (unreadable on every transport), previdian (listing 403), baselland.ch FAQ (403 to the container; read through the canton's short link).

2026-11-22T0355Z-intel · Sonnet 5.5 · window 26 h · 1 entry published

Verification & coverage notes

Window 26 h (gap 24.00 h to 2026-11-21T0355Z-intel, class Standard). A weekend window that was almost empty at source: one new entry and five changelog records (two reader-facing updates, three improvements), no deep dive, no critical. The will-publish set was 11 items, over the ~8 a main-agent deep read should carry; the main agent read the primaries itself (22 pages through extract, saved under work/2026-11-22T0355Z-intel/bodies/) because every one was a vendor page or a single research post.

  • KEV sweep: no CISA KEV addition inside the window (catalog 2026.11.20 is the newest, released 2026-11-20 17:48 UTC) and no ransomware-flag row; nothing to disposition. S1 re-ran cisa-kev and agrees.
  • Backlog: the file had no open row; nothing carried.
  • Priority calls: MONAI Label is notable, not high (a niche research server with no stated Swiss deployment). No priority moved on any updated entry. Relevance clause for MONAI Label: it clears PD-11 (b), an exploited flaw (CVE-2026-133968, fixed in 0.8.6 on 2026-11-22), for the exposure class of public universities and university hospitals that run research imaging tooling; the entry carries no source stating a Swiss deployment, so it is held to notable. The first composition read the project's advisory page, which still said the fix would ship in the next release, and missed the 0.8.6 release and the CVE that predate the run; verifier iteration 1 caught it and the entry was rewritten around both.
  • Single-source: none among the published items beyond the project advisory plus Amazon pair for MONAI Label (multi-source, credibility 2).
  • Updates: nginx2root (update) gained Cisco advisory version 1.1 (UCS Director now affected; Unified CCX, Finesse and more listed), Fortinet's not-impacted list of 2026-11-21 (FortiOS, FortiProxy, FortiMail not impacted, 51 names under investigation) Ubuntu's USN-9159-1 and Synology's SA-26:20 (DSM affected by CVE-2026-123007, fixed builds 7.4.1-90080-2 and 7.3.2-86009-6, own action line). Ruby2Shell (update) gained GitLab's critical patch release 19.6.1, 19.5.8 and 19.4.10 and Veria Labs' revised table (Chatwoot patched, GitHub Enterprise Server the one unfixed product); its action list gained a GitLab line. Java4Shell, the Cisco Secure Email Gateway CVE-2026-76519 entry (public Metasploit module, one summary clause added) and Basel-Landschaft (first-phase facts, Alertswiss warning) are improvement records: the facts they add are dated before the window (the Debian fixes for Java4Shell are dated 2026-11-19), so none re-floats its entry.
  • borderline-drop (PD-7, out-of-window, composed and withdrawn): Synology SA-26:20 and SA-26:21 (S1), CVE-2026-120382, an unauthenticated CVSS 9.8 argument-injection flaw in the DSM OAuth API with arbitrary file read and write, plus the nginx2root flaw in DSM; fixed in DSM 7.4.1-90080-2 and 7.3.2-86009-6, DSM 7.2.x, 7.1 and BeeStation OS still ongoing; published 2026-11-19, revised 2026-11-20 08:25 UTC. The same source was swept by the previous fire, so this is a missed item, not a between-sweeps case, and the exception for a rotational lookback does not apply. SA-26:20 (the nginx flaw in DSM) was added to the nginx2root entry; SA-26:21 and its CVE-2026-120382 stay out and are the strongest lead for the audit's G3 sweep: compose-ready detail in findings.S1.yaml item 1.
  • borderline-drop (PD-7): Huntress on timeroasting detection (2026-11-19), Unit 42 on Com-affiliated vishing (2026-11-20) and Kaspersky's Operation ShadowCloud, two parts (2026-11-17) (S3), all three came from the standing major-lab check, not from a slice record, and S3's lookback: true flag did not apply because those publishers' records were not in its slice; the previous fire already dropped Unit 42 as incremental to three UNC6671 entries and listed the other two as leads. Compose-ready detail is in findings.S3.yaml items 2 to 4 for the audit.
  • borderline-drop: Talos UAT-12643 and Kaspersky AuditTeam OpsAgent (S3), out of window and crimeware with no public-sector nexus; Check Point State of Ransomware Q3 (statistics); TrendAI BYOD ransomware (low confidence, single source); Microsoft 365 outage-themed phishing lure (no compromise, no actor); React2STEAL (long-patched flaws, single analysis); Microsoft device-code Copilot CLI research (lab proof of concept, no in-the-wild use).
  • borderline-drop: WatchGuard Dimension 2.3.2 (S1), 15 advisories, one unauthenticated log-collection RCE at CVSS 9.3, published 2026-11-19, no exploitation, internal log service with no stated exposure; WordPress 7.1.5, the CERT-FR batch of 2026-11-20 (Metabase, Tenable Security Center, Tomcat, WS_FTP), the EUVD open-source batch, Mitel MX-ONE MISA-2026-0011 and the Zimbra Metasploit modules, no exploitation or out of window.
  • borderline-drop: BSI Lagebericht 2026 (S2, annual report), Germany-only statistics published 2026-11-19; CSIRT Italia October operational summary (statistics, Italy); BundID two-factor confirmation (delta dated 2026-11-16 and 17); Publica's external governance review and its test-environment statement (governance only, no new vector, already in the entry through PKZH's statement); European Commission ARTEX incident (S2, S4), already in the ARTEX entry's 2026-11-20 record.
  • borderline-drop: Microsoft Entra Connect Health tenant-metadata exposure (S4), fixed server-side with no customer action, single second-hand source; Bell Canada agentic intruder and Rackspace Spot credential abuse (single source each, no Swiss nexus); N-able Mail Assure, FBI NCIC, USDA, FIFA leak-site claim, France Travail and other French SME notices, SBC Medical, iQSTEL, Nvidia, TfL, NSA outage, Threema audit and the Concevis release (no vector, no nexus or not an incident).
  • Slice completion: every slice record of the four domains has a ledger row (S1 26, S2 19, S3 14, S4 10; 69 of 69 attempted); no continuation was needed. rapid7-research was in S1's slice; the major-lab sources and synology-security-advisories were read outside the slices and are not counted as attempted. 90 sources were excluded from the allocation by the previous two fires' attempts; the rotation cursor ranked the slices.
  • Source health: 335 of 335 probed; three flags fixed in this run (ox-security read through its feed, lumen-black-lotus-labs through its query index, cdt-ch-ticino marked general-news) and the second pass left no unsolved source.
  • Sources: candidates added ubuntu-usn (S1) and bsi-press (S2); synology-security-advisories gained its verified RSS feed; recipe and health notes for lab52, sygnia, hadrian-labs (third marketing-only sweep: demotion candidate) and watchguard-psirt. last_successful_fetch moved only for the three slice sources whose content was used (fortinet-psirt, rapid7-research, csa-labs) so outside-slice checks do not advance a rotation cursor.
  • Entity registry: seven product entities added; the registry file is about 760 KB and was searched with grep, not read whole. No relation edge added.
  • Note for the next audit: the process note from S4 holds: headline-level dedup misses material that sits only in a covered entry's records or body (the European Commission detail was in the ARTEX entry's update section); the Java4Shell, nginx2root and Ruby2Shell entries' main analyses were left at their earlier length and their bodies grew by one section each.
  • Coverage gaps: lab52 (feed SSL reset; one metered-reader read); baselland.ch media listing (403 on every transport); databreaches.net article bodies (403); sygnia.co (extract and url fail, WebFetch reads it); psirt.watchguard.com is the working WatchGuard detail host; Reddit unreachable.
  • Verification: three iterations, all NEEDS_FIXES. Iteration 1 returned truth 9, editorial 5, advisory 3; the blocking finding was that the MONAI Label entry told readers there was no CVE and no fixed release, when MONAI Label 0.8.6 (2026-11-22 01:29 UTC) and CVE-2026-133968 (2026-11-20) already existed; the entry was rewritten around both. The other findings were attribution and citation-date slips (a Cisco table row listed as new that the entry already carried, a weakness name cited to a page that does not use it, a Veria Labs date, the Basel cut-off attributed to the wrong statement), the Ubuntu Pro caveat and a missing Synology DSM row on the nginx2root entry. Iteration 2 returned truth 3, editorial 1, advisory 2 with one F4 (the Basel summary listed nationality where the canton's list says civil status). Iteration 3 returned truth 2, editorial 0, advisory 1 and no F1 or F4, so the run published on the low-residual early exit after applying all three remediations; the final counter reads the two truth findings of that iteration, both fixed before commit. Declined across iterations: Synology SA-26:21 and CVE-2026-120382 stay out (out of window, no exploitation, source swept by the previous fire; the DSM builds that carry its fix are on the nginx2root entry), and five Basel claims that rest on the canton FAQ page, which returns 403 to every verifier pass and is unchanged text from the previous fire.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-11-21
item.description:
• Arctic Wolf: a cleared Windows event log keeps earlier records in its first EVTX chunk; carve it. Arctic Wolf incident responders report that clearing a Windows event log truncates the EVTX file after the first 64 KB cluster and resets the record numbers, but the first chunk keeps its earlier records in its free space. On a domain controller the System log held 104 allocated events after the final clear, yet the encryptor's full command line, stamped about three hours before the clear, sat inside the allocated file, and Event Viewer, EvtxECmd and Magnet AXIOM showed none of it; a PowerShell log in a second case held 44 records of which one was allocated. →
  • Rapid7: Webworm hides SoftEther VPN Bridge behind NtMonitor branding, new endpoints and an encrypted config. Rapid7 describes NtMonitor, a Windows build of SoftEther VPN Bridge 4.44 that it attributes with moderate confidence to Webworm, the China-aligned actor that ESET documented moving to European government targets in May 2026. The rebuild keeps SoftEther's function of bridging a remote network into the victim's LAN and strips its fingerprints: branding, handshake paths, the handshake watermark, the separate resource archive and the plain-text configuration are all changed, and Rapid7 found no backdoor or other added capability. Only one antivirus vendor detected the sample on VirusTotal although it has been public since January. →
  • SAP Enterprise Portal JNDI injection from November 2025 is now on CISA KEV; confirm Security Note 3660969 is applied. CISA added CVE-2025-42884 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20 on evidence of active exploitation it does not describe. The flaw lets an unauthenticated attacker inject JNDI environment properties or a URL used in a JNDI lookup in SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal (EP-BASIS and EP-RUNTIME 7.50) and read or modify server information; SAP rated it Medium, CVSS 3.1 6.5, and fixed it with Security Note 3660969 on its November 2025 Patch Day. No source names an actor, a victim or how it is chained. →

TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01Arctic Wolf: a cleared Windows event log keeps earlier records in its first EVTX chunk; carve it. Arctic Wolf incident responders report that clearing a Windows event log truncates the EVTX file after the first 64 KB cluster and resets the record numbers, but the first chunk keeps its earlier records in its free space.   2. 02Rapid7: Webworm hides SoftEther VPN Bridge behind NtMonitor branding, new endpoints and an encrypted config. Rapid7 describes NtMonitor, a Windows build of SoftEther VPN Bridge 4.44 that it attributes with moderate confidence to Webworm, the China-aligned actor that ESET documented moving to European government targets in May 2026. The rebuild keeps SoftEther's function of bridging a remote network into the victim's LAN and strips its fingerprints: branding, handshake paths, the handshake watermark, the separate resource archive and the plain-text configuration are all changed, and Rapid7 found no backdoor or other added capability. Only one antivirus vendor detected the sample on VirusTotal although it has been public since January. →
  3. 03SAP Enterprise Portal JNDI injection from November 2025 is now on CISA KEV; confirm Security Note 3660969 is applied. CISA added CVE-2025-42884 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20 on evidence of active exploitation it does not describe. The flaw lets an unauthenticated attacker inject JNDI environment properties or a URL used in a JNDI lookup in SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal (EP-BASIS and EP-RUNTIME 7.50) and read or modify server information; SAP rated it Medium, CVSS 3.1 6.5, and fixed it with Security Note 3660969 on its November 2025 Patch Day. No source names an actor, a victim or how it is chained. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 3Trending vulnerabilities 2Research, reports & policy 1Updates to prior coverage 5Action items 7

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures3 items

NOTABLENATOB3

Webworm's NtMonitor: Rapid7 finds a custom rebuild of the SoftEther VPN Bridge that removes the open-source tool's detection fingerprints (rebranded metadata, renamed handshake endpoints, a custom handshake watermark, an embedded resource archive and an encrypted configuration), attributed with moderate confidence to the China-aligned actor that targets European governments

Rapid7 analysed what it believes is a so-far unknown custom tool, a modified build of SoftEther VPN Bridge version 4.44 (build 9807) that it attributes to Webworm with moderate confidence (Rapid7, 2026-11-19). Webworm is the China-aligned actor that ESET reported in May 2026 moving to European government targets and to dual-use tools such as SoftEther (ESET Research, 2026-05-20). The rebuild keeps the bridge function, which cascades a remote network into the victim's local network, and removes the fingerprints: the PE metadata and internal strings are rebranded as a network-monitoring product (inconsistently, since the service name and many registry paths still say SoftEther), the HTTP handshake endpoints get update-style names, the handshake watermark becomes a truncated PNG header so stock SoftEther peers cannot connect and the stock watermark cannot fingerprint the build, the resource archive that normally sits beside the executable is embedded in it as a PE resource, and the configuration is stored under a new name in a custom-encrypted format (Rapid7, 2026-11-19). Rapid7 found no backdoor or other added capability, concludes the actor puts stealth above capability, and says only one antivirus vendor detected the sample although it has been public since January (Rapid7, 2026-11-19).

Exposure
Windows hosts in government networks that Webworm has already compromised; Rapid7 says that in every configuration it holds the VPN is set to bridge a remote network into the local one (Rapid7, 2026-11-19).
Detection
Rapid7's most reliable network detection, where TLS traffic can be inspected, is a POST request to an update-themed CGI path with a JPEG content type whose body starts with a PNG file header; on hosts, look for a SoftEther VPN Bridge service that was not installed by the organisation, in particular one whose binary carries its resource archive inside itself, and for firewall rules added by such a service (Rapid7, 2026-11-19). Rapid7 calls the branding the easiest change for the actor to make next and says the endpoints and watermark can be swapped out trivially, so behaviour that is intrinsic to SoftEther matters more than any one string (Rapid7, 2026-11-19).
Defender takeaway
Government networks in Europe should treat any unmanaged SoftEther VPN Bridge, however it is named, as a persistence mechanism that bridges an outside network into theirs, and learn the tool's intrinsic behaviour, as Rapid7 recommends for the government sector (Rapid7, 2026-11-19).

Builds on: 2026-05-21/webworm-china-aligned-shifts-to-eu-government-targets-echocr

threat21 Nov 04:49Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Rapid7 · ESET Research
ROUTINEupdatedNATOA2

Canton Basel-Landschaft: attackers took about 97,000 records from a database of work permits for cross-border commuters (permit G) in the cyberattack on the cantonal administration; the canton cannot say which records, assumes all, and names no entry point or actor

A confirmed data theft from a Swiss cantonal administration: the canton of Basel-Landschaft said on 2026-11-20 that forensic analysis showed the attackers reached a database of work permits for cross-border commuters (permit G) and took about 97,000 records for applications lodged through its online platform since 2016-11-28 (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-20). It cannot establish which records were taken and assumes all, took the platform off the network, filed a criminal complaint against unknown persons and names no entry point, tool or actor (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-20; Polizeiticker, 2026-11-20), after other cantonal applications had been switched off earlier in the week (Inside IT, 2026-11-20).

Exposure
Persons for whom a permit-G application was lodged, renewed or changed through the cantonal platform since 2016-11-28, and the contact persons of their employers in the canton; the database kept completed procedures too, so people whose permits ended are affected as well (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-20). The canton cannot exclude that uploaded documents such as contracts or ID copies were taken but has no indication of it (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-20).
Defender takeaway
An online application platform that keeps every historic procedure puts the whole archive in play when it is reached, so check how much completed data your own citizen-facing and supplier-run platforms retain; employers of cross-border commuters in the canton should expect phishing and social engineering that quotes correct personal details, because the canton warns that such messages can be built from the stolen data (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-20).
Improvement22 Nov 2026 04:35 UTCrun 2026-11-22T0355Z-intelsourcessourcing_notebodysummary

The canton's media release of Wednesday 2026-11-18 says diverse attacks on the cantonal IT had run since Sunday 2026-11-15, that individual servers had to be isolated from the internet and that further measures would be announced through the AlertSwiss app (translated from German) (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-18). Its update of that evening, relayed by Keystone-SDA, counts about twenty applications on six servers being reinstalled and says the IT of the rescue and security organisations was never affected; the Alertswiss warning of the night that the emergency numbers 112, 117 and 118 might be restricted was withdrawn a few hours later, and a government spokesperson said the numbers had stayed reachable and the warning was issued as a precaution (watson.ch, 2026-11-18).

incident21 Nov 04:47Zsingle-source · victim disclosureOpen finding →
Sources: Canton Basel-Landschaft (FAQ-Data page) · Canton Basel-Landschaft (media release on the attack) · Polizeiticker Schweiz (relays the canton's communiqué) · Inside IT · watson.ch (Keystone-SDA)
ROUTINENATOA2

Hokkaido: resident-register, support-needed and tax data of the cities of Rumoi and Iwamizawa and the town of Shintoku sat on a subcontractor's development PC infected with the K2F information stealer, which GIS Hokkaido links to the NIKKE game launcher; Rumoi's data was still there after its contract ended

Three Hokkaido municipalities disclosed on 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-19 that personal data they had handed to their contractor GIS Hokkaido was stored on a development terminal of GIS Hokkaido's subcontractor Rimgate, on which traces of the information stealer K2F were found: the terminal was infected overnight on 2 to 3 November, Rimgate found the traces on 4 November and cut it from the network, and GIS Hokkaido told the municipalities between 13 and 16 November (Rumoi City, 2026-11-19; Iwamizawa City, 2026-11-18; Shintoku Town, 2026-11-18). The data at risk is up to 71,002 resident-register records (as of February 2022) and 4,503 records of people needing support, with disability category and care level, for Rumoi, whose personal data was still on the terminal after its contract ended; 6,001 resident-register and 986 disaster-evacuation-support records for Shintoku; and up to 10,348 land parcels and 7,037 buildings of fixed-asset-tax data for Iwamizawa; none contains the national My Number and no leak or misuse is confirmed (translated from Japanese) (Rumoi City, 2026-11-19; Iwamizawa City, 2026-11-18; Shintoku Town, 2026-11-18). GIS Hokkaido told ITmedia that the PC launcher of the game NIKKE is involved and declined to say whether Rimgate staff ran the game on the work PC; ITmedia adds that a third-party tampering with that launcher, which could deliver K2F on start, became public on 5 November (translated from Japanese) (ITmedia NEWS, 2026-11-19). This is municipal public-sector data held through a supplier chain.

Exposure
Any administration whose resident, social-care or tax data went to a contractor that subcontracts, and any supplier endpoint where consumer software such as a game launcher can run next to project data; the check is which supplier terminals still hold extracts from finished projects (Rumoi City, 2026-11-19; ITmedia NEWS, 2026-11-19).
Detection
The infection path is the observable: a consumer game launcher on a workstation that holds project data, and, because K2F steals passwords and allows remote control, password-store reads by non-browser processes and unexplained remote sessions on such machines; the sources give no more specific indicator (ITmedia NEWS, 2026-11-19).
Defender takeaway
Ask each supplier and its subcontractors which of your extracts they still hold, have them delete data of finished contracts and confirm it, and keep consumer software off the machines that handle it; Rumoi's contract had ended yet its data was still on the infected terminal (Rumoi City, 2026-11-19).
incident21 Nov 04:48Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Rumoi City (municipal notice, Japanese) · Iwamizawa City (municipal notice, Japanese) · Shintoku Town (municipal notice, Japanese) · ITmedia NEWS (Japanese)

02Trending vulnerabilities2 items

NOTABLECVE-2025-42884exploitedNATOA3

CVE-2025-42884, SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal EP-BASIS and EP-RUNTIME 7.50: a JNDI injection that an unauthenticated attacker can use to read or change server information, fixed by SAP Security Note 3660969 in November 2025 and listed by CISA as exploited on 2026-11-20 (CVSS 3.1 6.5)

CISA added CVE-2025-42884 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20, naming SAP NetWeaver, on evidence of active exploitation that it does not describe (CISA, 2026-11-20). The flaw is a year old: SAP's November 2025 Patch Day lists a JNDI injection in SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal, EP-BASIS 7.50 and EP-RUNTIME 7.50, fixed by Security Note 3660969 at priority Medium and CVSS 6.5 (SAP, 2025-11-11). ENISA's record describes an unauthenticated attacker who injects JNDI environment properties or passes a URL used during a JNDI lookup, reaching an unintended JNDI provider, which could lead to disclosure or modification of information about the server, with no impact on availability, and it marks exploitation from 2026-11-20 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-20). No source names an actor, a victim or the way the flaw is chained.

Exposure
SAP NetWeaver AS Java with Enterprise Portal, components EP-BASIS and EP-RUNTIME 7.50; whether it is fixed depends on Security Note 3660969 being implemented, and the note text is behind SAP's login (SAP, 2025-11-11).
Detection
Web access logs of the portal for requests that carry JNDI environment properties or lookup URLs from unauthenticated sources, and outbound connections from the portal's server to hosts it does not normally contact, which a lookup to an attacker-chosen provider would produce; no source publishes an indicator or a post-compromise check (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-20).
Defender takeaway
Confirm Security Note 3660969 is implemented on every Enterprise Portal 7.50 system and apply it where it is not; the listing shows the year-old flaw is being used, though no source says against whom or with what effect (CISA, 2026-11-20).
vulnerability21 Nov 04:46Zsingle-source · national CERTOpen finding →
Sources: CISA · SAP Security Patch Day bulletins 2025 · ENISA EUVD (EUVD-2025-60994)
NOTABLECVE-2026-129448 +1exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-129448, Apache Roller 4.0.0 to 6.1.5: an unauthenticated request to the XML-RPC endpoint deserializes attacker-controlled objects before authentication and runs code on the server; Apache says it is being exploited, CISA lists it, fixed in 6.1.6 (CVSS 3.1 9.8)

Apache's announcement of 2026-11-17 assigns CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 3.1 9.8) to Apache Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 and says "This issue is being actively exploited" (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17). It is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which Apache disclosed on 2026-09-25 for 6.1.5 only (Apache via oss-security, 2026-09-25). Roller's XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17); the servlet is mapped unconditionally, so the request is parsed even when the XML-RPC feature is switched off and no non-default configuration is needed (Apache via oss-security, 2026-09-25). CISA added CVE-2026-129448 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20 (CISA, 2026-11-20), and Apache has not said who is exploiting it or how many servers are compromised (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-18). Roller 6.1.6 or later disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the feature is off, and the project's downloads page offers 6.1.7 as the best available release (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17; Apache Roller, 2026-11-21).

Exposure
Any Apache Roller from 4.0.0 to 6.1.5 whose /roller-services/xmlrpc path is reachable, including sites where XML-RPC was switched off in the administration interface; the checks are the deployed version and the enabledForExtensions setting in WEB-INF/web.xml, both of which Apache names (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17). Roller is a niche Java group-blogging server with a much smaller market share than mainstream blogging platforms (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Web access and reverse-proxy logs for POST requests to /roller-services/xmlrpc from unfamiliar sources, and child processes started by the Java application server's account, since the flaw runs attacker-chosen code; Apache's announcement names no indicator and no post-compromise check, and an upgrade does not undo an earlier compromise (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade to 6.1.6 or later now; where that waits, Apache's interim steps are setting enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml or removing the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping, then restarting (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17). Treat an exposed instance on an older release as possibly compromised, because Apache and CISA report exploitation (CISA, 2026-11-20).

03Research, reports & policy1 item

NOTABLENATOB3

Cleared Windows event logs are not empty: Arctic Wolf shows that clearing an EVTX log truncates it after the first 64 KB cluster and leaves the earlier records in that chunk's free space, where standard forensic tools do not parse or flag them, and recovered a ransomware encryptor's command line this way

Arctic Wolf's incident responders report that clearing a Windows event log does not wipe the underlying EVTX file (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20). On clearing, Windows truncates the file after the first 64 KB cluster and resets the first and last record numbers, but that first chunk keeps its earlier records in free space until enough new events fill it (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20). In a ransomware case the encryptor needed a password argument to run, and Arctic Wolf found its full command line inside the allocated System.EVTX of a domain controller, stamped about three hours before the final clear and absent from the parsed output of Event Viewer, EvtxECmd and Magnet AXIOM; another log held a netscan execution record and an attacker hostname that survived the same way (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20). In a second case a PowerShell log held 44 records of which one was allocated, all of them the same command that clears every log, which shows repeated clearing (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20). Arctic Wolf identified no forensic tool that flags records left in the slack space after a clear, and records come back with some template-held fields missing (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20).

Detection
The clearing itself is the alertable event, since Arctic Wolf notes that it often triggers EDR or IDS alerting and is frequently what exposes an attack in progress; the recovery step is forensic: when a log shows as cleared, acquire the EVTX file and carve its first chunk for records with earlier timestamps and lower record identifiers than the allocated ones (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20).
Defender takeaway
Do not treat a cleared log as empty; preserve the EVTX files of affected hosts promptly, because new events overwrite the free space once they fill the first 64 KB, and search the whole file, not only the parsed events, for the encryptor's command line, tool names and hostnames (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20).

Iteration 1 returned truth 7, editorial 3 (one F4: an inverted record-identifier statement in the EVTX Detection line); iteration 2 returned truth 5 (one F4: a BSI quote the live PDF no longer carried, because the URL now serves version 1.1); iteration 3 returned truth 2, editorial 0, advisory 3 and no F1 or F4, so the run published on the low-residual early exit with both residuals fixed in place. Last-minute fixes after iteration 3 (the Danfoss record summary wording, one run-record note, one Danfoss section sentence, markdown asterisks in a quote's original) were not re-verified by a fourth pass. No entry was dropped. The wombat@127.0.0.1 Erlang node name in the Cisco entry was flagged three times as borderline against the no-IOC rule and kept: F6 publishes it as the log marker of a successful exploit, and it is not a hash, address or attacker domain.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-11-20
item.description:
• Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13, 3.3.14 fix seven memory flaws; Veria's Rails exploit not found yet: update the interpreter. The Ruby project released 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14 on 2026-11-18 for seven memory-corruption flaws in the regexp engine and in string case conversion, three rated Critical, and says it knows of proofs of concept that reach remote code execution. Veria Labs, which found the case-conversion flaw independently (CVE-2026-132825, a one-byte heap overflow), says Rails and classic-style Sinatra are exposed without authentication in their default configuration and announced a code-execution proof of concept on stock Rails for 25 November 2026, which its page, blog feed and GitHub organisation did not show as released on 2026-11-27; no exploitation is reported. GitHub Enterprise Server and older GitLab branches now carry the fix. Ruby 3.2 and earlier are end of life, and the interpreter itself, not a gem, must be updated. →
  • vCenter auth bypass exploited since September; Metasploit module in public review: patch to 9.1.2, 9.0.2.0300 or 8.0 U3m. Broadcom's advisory VMSA-2026-0009 of 2026-11-19 fixes CVE-2026-123890, an authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service of vCenter that needs only network access to vCenter (CVSS 3.1 9.8), with no workaround and, in Broadcom's words, an emergency change. Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant say ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus actor, exploited it from early September 2026 to move from a compromised remote-support appliance to vCenter, forge administrator SAML sessions and extract domain-controller data from guest virtual disks on ESXi; Broadcom's advisory does not state exploitation. Fixed builds for this flaw are 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200, 9.1.1.0200 and VMware Cloud Foundation 5.2.5, but a second Directory Service bypass fixed on 2026-11-24 leaves 9.1.1.0200 and 9.0.2.0200 affected (9.1.2, 9.0.2.0300 and 8.0 U3m cover both). Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis and a Metasploit module is in a public pull request; vCenter 7.0 has no public fix. →
  • Mitel OpenScape 4000: two unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 Platform flaws; upgrade to V11 R2.14 or restrict access. Mitel's advisory MISA-2026-0013 of 2026-11-18 covers three flaws in the Platform component of OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager: an unauthenticated improper-authentication flaw and an unauthenticated command injection, both CVSS 3.1 10.0, and a command injection reachable from the adjacent network (9.6). The CVE Program published CVE-2026-137724, CVE-2026-137721 and CVE-2026-137723 on 2026-11-27, ids that Mitel's advisory does not yet list; the fix is V11 R2.14, PLT HF5 on V11 R1.26 or a patch for V10 R0.28 to V11 R0.22, and enabling Security Mode restricted access is Mitel's workaround. The advisory says nothing about exploitation. →

Active threats, incidents & disclosures 1Trending vulnerabilities 4Updates to prior coverage 6Action items 10

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures1 item

ROUTINEupdatedNATOB2

Università della Svizzera italiana (USI, Lugano): third parties exploited a vulnerability in an online-forms system and had access to form responses and attached documents from 9 to 17 November 2026, mainly contact details, and more than 8,000 e-mails warned those concerned; USI names no product or actor

USI said on 2026-11-19 that unauthorised third parties had access to data held on one of its applications between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-17, by exploiting a vulnerability in the software of an online-forms system that the university uses to collect certain job applications, scholarship requests and surveys (USI via Corriere del Ticino, 2026-11-19). The affected server held the responses to the forms and their attached documents; USI's IT services secured it, USI informed the competent authorities and the people whose data may be affected, and it says the causes and the risk to those concerned are still being checked, which will take several more weeks (USI via laRegione, 2026-11-19). It names no product, vulnerability or attacker, and Ticinonline adds that it is not yet clear when the intrusion began or how long it lasted (Ticinonline, 2026-11-19).

Defender takeaway
Check any forms, survey or application-intake system, your own or a supplier's, that stores uploaded documents, and treat those documents as exposed on a system that was reachable with vulnerable software during the access window of 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-17 (USI via laRegione, 2026-11-19).
Update21 Nov 2026 04:40 UTCrun 2026-11-21T0355Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

In an interview of 2026-11-20 USI's chief operating officer said the stolen data are essentially names, e-mail addresses and phone numbers and only to a minimal extent job applications or scholarship requests, that the forms software also serves event management, and that more than 8,000 e-mails warned those concerned (translated from Italian) (Corriere del Ticino, 2026-11-20). He calls the attack the work of AI agents that scan the network for vulnerabilities, offers no technical evidence for that, and leaves the product and the vulnerability unnamed (translated from Italian) (Corriere del Ticino, 2026-11-20).

incident20 Nov 05:09Zsingle-source · victim disclosureOpen finding →
Sources: Corriere del Ticino (reproduces the USI communiqué) · laRegione (reproduces the USI communiqué) · Ticinonline · Corriere del Ticino (interview with the USI chief operating officer)

02Trending vulnerabilities4 items

HIGHCVE-2026-132825updatedNATOA2

Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14: seven memory-safety flaws in the regexp engine and string case conversion, three rated Critical by the project, with proofs of concept for code execution; Veria Labs says Rails and classic Sinatra are exposed by default and announces a public Rails exploit for 25 November 2026 (CVE-2026-132825, CVSS 3.1 7.4)

The Ruby project released 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14 on 2026-11-18 to fix seven vulnerabilities in the regexp engine and in string case conversion, and says it is aware of proofs of concept that prove some of them can be used to trigger remote code execution (Ruby project, 2026-11-18). NCSC.ch lists three as Critical, a one-byte heap overflow in case conversion of strings in single-byte encodings such as ISO-8859-1 and Windows-1252, a double free in regexp compilation and a heap overflow from an integer overflow in regexp compilation, and the rest as High or Moderate (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19); the project's advisory for the first confirms it can write one byte past the output buffer (Ruby project, 2026-11-18). Affected are Ruby 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0 to 3.4.12 and 4.0.0 to 4.0.9, and Ruby 3.2 and earlier are end of life and unfixed (Ruby project, 2026-11-18).

NCSC.ch says Rails and classic-style Sinatra are exposed to the case-conversion overflow in their default configuration (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19); watchTowr reports no exploitation as of 2026-11-19 (watchTowr, 2026-11-19). Veria Labs, which says it found the flaw independently and first demonstrated code execution, calls it Ruby2Shell, says it is reachable without authentication on Rails and classic Sinatra and that plain Rack and other frameworks are not exposed by default, and announced a proof of concept for remote code execution on stock Rails for 25 November 2026, or later if major vendors have not shipped a fix; its page, blog feed and GitHub organisation showed no release on 2026-11-27 (Veria Labs, 2026-11-19). Moritz Sanft, a co-discoverer Veria names, writes that a plain Rails application is enough to be exploitable and that OpenAI sent the Ruby maintainers working exploit proofs on 2026-11-07 (Durendal, 2026-11-19). GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22.6 (GitHub, 2026-11-22), 3.21.11 (GitHub, 2026-11-22), 3.20.13 (GitHub, 2026-11-22) and 3.19.17 (GitHub, 2026-11-22) carry the Ruby fix, although Veria's table, last changed on 2026-11-21, still shows 3.22.5 and earlier unfixed; it lists Chatwoot (4.20.1), GitLab, Mastodon, OpenProject and the Discourse base image as patched, and the Ruby advisories name no product, so the vendors' own advisories decide for each (Veria Labs, 2026-11-19). CVE-2026-132825 names the case-conversion overflow and is scored CVSS 3.1 7.4 with a local attack vector and high complexity (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-19); the Ruby announcement says CVE identifiers were requested and none was assigned at publication, so the other six flaws are known by GHSA id (Ruby project, 2026-11-18).

Exposure
Ruby 3.3, 3.4 and 4.0 below the fixed releases that run Rails or classic Sinatra, or any application that passes untrusted text to a case-changing method or compiles untrusted regexp patterns; the interpreter version is shown by ruby -v, and self-hosted products that bundle Ruby carry their own fix timeline (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19).
Detection
Crashes, segmentation faults and abnormal restarts of Ruby application workers that coincide with requests carrying long single-byte-encoded text or unusual regexp parameters, and a shell or network tool spawned by a Ruby worker process.
Defender takeaway
Update the interpreter, not the gems, rebuild container images and restart workers, since exploit proofs exist and Veria's proof of concept may appear at any time; until then NCSC.ch's temporary measures are to avoid compiling regexps from untrusted input and, for the case-conversion flaw, to convert input to UTF-8 so the vulnerable path is not reached (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19).
Update22 Nov 2026 04:32 UTCrun 2026-11-22T0355Z-intelaffected_productsentitiessourcesevidenceactionsbody

GitLab released 19.6.1, 19.5.8 and 19.4.10 on 2026-11-20 as a critical patch release for self-managed installations, with CVE-2026-132825 as its only security fix; GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already patched (GitLab, 2026-11-20). The fix is a patch to Ruby: official Linux packages and container images already carry it, while a self-compiled installation must rebuild Ruby 3.3.14 or 3.4.13 or a later release of the same series, and the release also covers the other flaws in the Ruby advisory (GitLab, 2026-11-20). Veria Labs' software table now lists Chatwoot 4.20.0 and earlier as fixed in 4.20.1, leaving GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22.5 and earlier as the one product shown without a fixed release, and its proof of concept for stock Rails is still announced for 25 November 2026, or later if major vendors have not shipped a fix (Veria Labs, 2026-11-19).

Update27 Nov 2026 04:57 UTCrun 2026-11-27T0355Z-intelheadlinesummaryaffected_productsentitiessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbodyupdated_at

GitHub's release notes list the Ruby update as a critical fix in GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22.6 (GitHub, 2026-11-22), 3.21.11 (GitHub, 2026-11-22), 3.20.13 (GitHub, 2026-11-22) and 3.19.17 (GitHub, 2026-11-22), all dated 2026-11-22, with application-level mitigations where an update was not immediately possible; they name no Ruby version or CVE. GitLab's release of 2026-11-25 backports the Ruby fix, a bump to Ruby 3.3.14 and 3.4.13, to 19.3.10, 19.2.11, 19.1.11, 19.0.12 and 18.11.15, which it calls an exception to its maintenance policy (GitLab, 2026-11-25).

Veria Labs' Rails proof of concept was announced for 2026-11-25 or later; its page, blog feed and GitHub organisation show no release as of 2026-11-27, which does not show that no exploit exists. Sanft writes that Rack's multipart method override and a field charset reach the vulnerable case conversion in a plain Rails application, and that OpenAI sent the Ruby maintainers working exploit proofs for the case-conversion and an integer-overflow flaw on 2026-11-07; the second flaw is limited to Rack 3.2.1 and earlier (Durendal, 2026-11-19).

vulnerability20 Nov 05:07Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Ruby project · Ruby project (GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5) · NCSC.ch Cyber Security Hub · Veria Labs · watchTowr · ENISA EUVD (EUVD-2026-129481) · GitLab · GitLab (19.6.2) · GitHub Enterprise Server release notes · Durendal (Moritz Sanft)
HIGHCVE-2026-123890 +4exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-123890, VMware vCenter Server: an unauthenticated authentication bypass in the Directory Service gives an administrator session; GTIG reports the suspected China-nexus actor ARMORY CASTLE exploited it from early September, Broadcom lists no workaround; first fixed in 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200 and 9.1.1.0200, with 9.1.2 and 9.0.2.0300 now superseding the 9.x builds (CVSS 3.1 9.8)

Broadcom's advisory VMSA-2026-0009 of 2026-11-19 fixes CVE-2026-123890, an authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service of vCenter that needs only network access (CVSS 3.1 9.8), with no workaround; it does not state exploitation (Broadcom, 2026-11-19; Broadcom, 2026-11-19). Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant say ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus actor, exploited it from early September 2026 with its BONESAW utility, in one intrusion (GTIG, 2026-11-19); BleepingComputer notes Broadcom has not confirmed it (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-19), and CISA listed the flaw as exploited on 2026-11-20 (CISA, 2026-11-20).

The cause is a session-key disclosure over DCE/RPC in the rpc_srp_verifier service on TCP 2012: the SRP key getter checks neither that the caller authenticated nor that it owns the verifier, and the RPC context handles are predictable UUIDv1 values, so an attacker needs only network access to TCP 2012 and an existing SSO principal name (Rapid7, 2026-11-24). Rapid7 chained the administrator session to a root shell on vCenter 8.0.2.00400 and describes a Metasploit module for the whole chain that sits in an open public pull request (Rapid7, 2026-11-24; Metasploit pull request, 2026-11-20). In GTIG's intrusion the actor forged administrator SAML assertions after extracting the SAML signing key, switched SSH on through the appliance management API and reached ESXi hosts, where it planted an authorized_keys entry and extracted domain data from Windows guest disks (GTIG, 2026-11-19).

Fixes for this flaw: vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 and 8.0 U3m and VMware Cloud Foundation 5.2.5; vCenter 7.0 has no public fix (Broadcom, 2026-11-19). VMSA-2026-0011 of 2026-11-24 fixes a second Directory Service bypass, CVE-2026-123903, in 9.1.2 and 9.0.2.0300, so 9.1.1.0200 and 9.0.2.0200 leave it open while 8.0 U3m and 5.2.5 cover both (Broadcom, 2026-11-24).

Exposure
VCenter 7.0, 8.0, 9.0 and 9.1 before the fixed builds; the prerequisites are network access to TCP 2012 and a valid SSO principal name, and GTIG's actor reached vCenter from an internal Linux appliance, so exposure does not require an internet-facing vCenter (Rapid7, 2026-11-24; GTIG, 2026-11-19).
Detection
In network telemetry, repeated calls to operation 1 of the SRP helper interface on TCP 2012 with no RPC authentication verifier and context UUIDs that differ mainly in their timestamp fields (Rapid7, 2026-11-24), and sweeps of ports 2012, 5480 and 9080 from a Linux appliance that is not a management host (GTIG, 2026-11-19); in appliance logs, a database-transfer grant in the vmdird log, the SSH-settings request and a new local administrator in the vAPI endpoint access log and the SSH enablement itself in the appliance management log, then an SSH login followed by sudo (Rapid7, 2026-11-24); on ESXi, vpxuser or root logins, a new authorized_keys entry and a hidden directory on a VMFS volume (GTIG, 2026-11-19). A forged SAML session looks like an administrator session, and because BONESAW extracts the SAML signing key the compromise check covers SSO and local administrators, signing material and ESXi keys from early September on (GTIG, 2026-11-19).

Triage: a connection to TCP 2012 or an administrator SRP login alone proves nothing; the signal is the call pattern and log sequence above (Rapid7, 2026-11-24).

Defender takeaway
Treat the update as an emergency change and move 9.x vCenter straight to 9.1.2 or 9.0.2.0300, which cover this flaw and the second bypass; until then GTIG's hardening guidance drops inbound TCP 2012 from non-allowlisted addresses, tested first because the port carries SSO traffic (GTIG, 2026-11-19; Broadcom, 2026-11-24).
Improvement22 Nov 2026 14:57 UTCrun 2026-11-22T1407Z-auditaffected_productsbodycves

CISA listed CVE-2026-123890 as exploited on 2026-11-20 (CISA, 2026-11-20). GTIG ties the SSH enablement to the appliance management API, describes the Directory Service database being pulled through the directory service's RPC interface and the master key and credential file being read over SSH, and names no log in which those reads appear (GTIG, 2026-11-19). Broadcom lists VMware vSphere Foundation among the impacted products as well (Broadcom, 2026-11-19).

Update25 Nov 2026 04:46 UTCrun 2026-11-25T0356Z-intelactionsbodycvesevidenceheadlinesourcessummarytagstitle

Rapid7 published its technical analysis of CVE-2026-123890 on 2026-11-24: the SRP key getter checks neither authentication nor verifier ownership and its RPC context handles are predictable, the chain reaches a root shell on vCenter 8.0.2.00400, and a Metasploit module that does the whole chain is described (Rapid7, 2026-11-24). That module is in an open public pull request to Metasploit (Metasploit pull request, 2026-11-20). Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0011 of 2026-11-24 fixes a second Directory Service authentication bypass, CVE-2026-123903, in vCenter 9.1.2 and 9.0.2.0300; 8.0 U3m and VMware Cloud Foundation 5.2.5 already carry that fix, but 9.1.1.0200 and 9.0.2.0200, the builds named above for this flaw, do not (Broadcom, 2026-11-24).

Builds on: 2026-10-16/cve-2026-102764-beyondtrust-remote-support-zero-day · 2026-07-30/vmware-vmsa-2026-0006-vcenter-auth-bypass-vmxnet3-escape

vulnerability20 Nov 05:02Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Broadcom (VMSA-2026-0009) · Broadcom (VMSA-2026-0009 Q&A) · Google Threat Intelligence Group / Mandiant · BleepingComputer · CISA · Rapid7 · Metasploit (pull request) · Broadcom (VMSA-2026-0011 Q&A)
NOTABLECVE-2026-137724 +2updatedNATOA2

Mitel OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager, MISA-2026-0013: two unauthenticated flaws in the Platform component rated CVSS 3.1 10.0 (CVE-2026-137724 improper authentication, CVE-2026-137721 command injection) and an adjacent-network command injection (CVE-2026-137723, 9.6); fixed in V11 R2.14, Security Mode restricted access is the workaround, no exploitation stated

Mitel's advisory MISA-2026-0013 of 2026-11-18 covers three flaws in the Platform component of OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager, tracked by Mitel's internal ids, which the advisory page still lists without CVE ids (Mitel, 2026-11-18). MTLVULN-1785 is an unauthenticated improper-authentication flaw that gives unauthorized access and MTLVULN-1786 an unauthenticated command injection through insufficient parameter sanitization, both CVSS 3.1 10.0 with changed scope; MTLVULN-1793 is a command injection that an unauthenticated attacker with adjacent network access can use, scored 9.6 (Mitel, 2026-11-18). The CVE Program records published on 2026-11-27 map them as CVE-2026-137724 for MTLVULN-1785 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-27), CVE-2026-137721 for MTLVULN-1786 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-27) and CVE-2026-137723 for MTLVULN-1793 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-27). Affected are OpenScape 4000 V11 R0.22 through V11 R2.11 and V10 R1.68 and earlier, and OpenScape 4000 Manager V11 R0.22 through V11 R2.11 and V10 R1.34, R1.42, R1.54 and R1.68; Mitel does not assess end-of-support releases (Mitel, 2026-11-18).

The issues are corrected in V11 R2.14, Mitel provides PLT HF5 for V11 R1.26 and a patch for V10 R0.28 to V11 R0.22 (for the Manager, V10 R1.34 to V11 R0.22), and for customers who cannot apply the fix quickly, enabling Security Mode restricted access is a workaround that prevents exploitation, with the steps in a portal-only article (Mitel, 2026-11-18). CERT-FR lists the risks as remote arbitrary code execution, remote denial of service, policy bypass and loss of integrity and confidentiality, and BSI describes an attacker who can bypass safeguards, disclose information or run arbitrary commands in the context of the system (CERT-FR, 2026-11-19; BSI, 2026-11-19). Mitel's text does not mention exploitation.

Exposure
OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager at the releases above; the vulnerable component is the Platform, and the advisory does not say which of its interfaces are normally reachable (Mitel, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Unauthenticated access to the Platform component from hosts that are not administration or maintenance systems, and unexpected command execution on the platform; both follow from the improper-authentication and command-injection mechanisms, and the advisory gives no detection guidance.
Defender takeaway
Apply the fix for the release in use now; where that waits, turn on Security Mode restricted access, and read the affected range against CERT-FR's wording if the system runs R2.12 or R2.13 (Mitel, 2026-11-18; CERT-FR, 2026-11-19).
Improvement28 Nov 2026 04:42 UTCrun 2026-11-28T0355Z-intelbodycvesevidencesourcessourcing_notesummarytitle

The CVE Program published CVE ids for the three flaws on 2026-11-27, which Mitel's advisory, still at revision 1.0 on 2026-11-28, does not yet list. CVE-2026-137724 is MTLVULN-1785, the unauthenticated improper-authentication flaw (CVSS 3.1 10.0) (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-27); CVE-2026-137721 is MTLVULN-1786, the command injection (10.0) (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-27); and CVE-2026-137723 is MTLVULN-1793, the command injection from the adjacent network (9.6) (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-27). Each record's description ends with Mitel's internal id, so the pairing is stated and not inferred. The fixed releases and the Security Mode workaround are unchanged, and the page still says nothing about exploitation (Mitel, 2026-11-18).

Builds on: 2026-11-18/mitel-micollab-misa-2026-0012-awv-unauth-command-injection

vulnerability20 Nov 05:08Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Mitel (MISA-2026-0013) · CERT-FR (CERTFR-2026-AVI-1569) · BSI CERT-Bund (WID-SEC-2026-4685) · ENISA EUVD (CVE-2026-137724) · ENISA EUVD (CVE-2026-137721) · ENISA EUVD (CVE-2026-137723)
NOTABLECVE-2026-129289 +7updatedNATOA2

PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36: CVE-2026-129289 lets an unauthenticated request smuggle a second FastCGI request into PHP-FPM and run PHP code when the front end reuses FastCGI connections; the release also fixes the session flaw left open in October and follow-ups to an incomplete earlier fix (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

PHP released 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 and 8.6.0 on 2026-11-19, with up to 18 CVEs per branch (PHP, 2026-11-19). The most direct is CVE-2026-129289: when php://input was opened but not read to the end, PHP-FPM leaves the unread request bytes on a persistent FastCGI connection, so a malformed multipart body can place a second FastCGI request inside the first, and an unauthenticated attacker can bypass front-end routing and execute attacker-controlled PHP code with the privileges of the worker (PHP, 2026-11-19). It requires a front end that enables persistent backend connections and an application path that opens php://input without reading it fully; standard nginx and Apache configurations that close the FastCGI connection after each request are not affected by the demonstrated attack (PHP, 2026-11-19).

Two session flaws close the item the October release left open (watchTowr, 2026-11-20): CVE-2026-115560, where upload-progress session data is written in one serializer format and read in another, and CVE-2026-126714, where an interrupted write by the default files handler leaves a mixed old and new session file; both end in object injection and need an object gadget chain in the application (PHP, 2026-11-19; PHP, 2026-11-19). The fix for the first disables upload progress by default (PHP, 2026-11-19). CVE-2026-129481, a use-after-free of a stale session filename after an interrupted session shutdown, is in PHP's words an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-109619, the PHP2Shell flaw CISA has listed as exploited since 2026-10-26 (CISA, 2026-11-20), and affects PHP 8.3 and later, and CVE-2026-129182, for PHP 8.5 only, covers further scenarios after the 8.5.12 fix (PHP, 2026-11-19; PHP, 2026-11-19).

CVE-2026-129474, PHP 8.5 only, is exposed on the built-in defaults, because fatal error backtraces are on in 8.5 and the default includes arguments, and php.ini-production, which sets zend.exception_ignore_args=1, or fatal_error_backtraces=0 prevents the attack; PHP confirmed code execution on 8.5 (PHP, 2026-11-19). CVE-2026-129496 needs a startup diagnostic written through a file-based error_log in a non-thread-safe build (PHP, 2026-11-19). CVE-2026-129291, an epoll use-after-free in PHP-FPM, gives root from a worker where catch_workers_output is on and the FPM master runs as root (PHP, 2026-11-19). NCSC.ch lists exploitation as unknown with no public proof of concept referenced, and watchTowr reports none as of 2026-11-20 (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19; watchTowr, 2026-11-20).

Exposure
PHP 8.5 without php.ini-production settings is exposed to CVE-2026-129474 on the defaults, when an application path enters a magic method (PHP, 2026-11-19). For CVE-2026-129289, PHP-FPM servers whose front end keeps FastCGI backend connections open (nginx fastcgi_keep_conn on, Apache mod_proxy_fcgi enablereuse=on, HAProxy in FastCGI mode) and whose applications open php://input without consuming it, which the PHP advisory says some frameworks do; standard setups are outside the demonstrated attack (PHP, 2026-11-19). The session flaws need an object gadget chain in the application, and the version is shown by php -v on the host or in the container image.
Detection
In web and proxy access logs, malformed multipart/form-data bodies sent to endpoints whose application opens php://input without consuming it, followed by PHP execution that no logged request explains; in process telemetry, a shell or network tool spawned by the PHP-FPM worker, which follows from worker-level code execution.
Defender takeaway
Move the PHP runtime, not the CMS or its plugins, to the fixed build of its branch and restart PHP-FPM; where that waits, turn FastCGI connection reuse off (PHP, 2026-11-19). PHP 8.1 hosts need a newer branch for CVE-2026-129291 (PHP, 2026-11-19).

CISA lists only CVE-2026-115731, and exploitation of the second flaw is not established.

The same Perforce advisory fixed a second flaw, CVE-2026-115732, an authorization bypass in the certificate-name matching of Puppet's authorization library, scored CVSS 4.0 9.0: a CA-signed certificate whose name extends or shortens an authorised host name is authorised as that host (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-03). Neodyme's example is that an attacker who got a certificate for evil.target.lab.local can authenticate as target.lab.local, then fetch that host's catalog, which can carry configuration files with database credentials and API tokens, push spoofed facts and add exported resources (Neodyme, 2026-11-03). Where the CA autosigns, such a certificate can be requested for a name that does not exist yet, and OpenVox says autosign is not the default but is common in real deployments (OpenVox, 2026-11-03); NCSC.ch adds that in Puppet Enterprise the bypass also enables CA administration and remote command execution on managed nodes (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19).

The fix is in the same Puppet Enterprise builds and in Puppet Core 9.1.3 and 8.22.2 (SecurityWeek, 2026-11-18); OpenVox ships it in OpenVox Server 9.2.0 and 8.18.0 (OpenVox, 2026-11-03) and in OpenVoxDB 9.2.0 and 8.18.0 (oss-security, 2026-11-03). CISA's catalog entry covers only CVE-2026-115731 (CISA, 2026-11-17); NCSC.ch labels the pair actively exploited with a proof of concept available and lists a community report as an additional source (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19), while the report The Hacker News quotes describes a CVE-2026-115731 intrusion, so exploitation of CVE-2026-115732 itself is not established (The Hacker News, 2026-11-18). NCSC.ch's temporary measures are to disable certificate autosigning, enforce strong request validation, audit the issued certificates for colliding names and review the CA configuration for signs of compromise (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19).

  • borderline-drop: cPanel WP Toolkit proxy, single BSI relay, no CVE or conditions, vendor page unreadable
  • borderline-drop: Frappe GHSA-vwqr-4mjv-ffrm; exploited ITW but needs an authenticated portal user, email spoofing and attachment read only, no constituency nexus
  • borderline-drop: BSI Lagebericht 2026 (annual report), Germany-specific statistics, no Swiss figures, awareness only
  • borderline-drop: Canton Zug M365 policy, relaxation of an internal rule, no obligation change for other defenders
  • borderline-drop: nginx2root Swiss exposure counts (Risikomonitor via Netzwoche), banner-based, no primary
  • borderline-drop: depthfirst Narrow Grants, Wide Engines, patched CVEs on regular cycle, MySQL needs high privileges, Oracle needs Create Session, pre-login chain not reproduced, hardening advice generic
  • borderline-drop: React2STEAL, single source, attacker pipeline on GitHub, no defender decision beyond known React2Shell patching
  • borderline-drop: Phantom53/HavoX, victims US individuals and non-constituency regions, ClickFix chain commonplace
  • borderline-drop: Check Point State of Ransomware Q3 2026, outside window, statistics, no takeaway
  • borderline-drop: N-able Mail Assure intrusion, no vector, no data, no Swiss link
  • borderline-drop: Transport for London photocard breach, UK, no vector, no Swiss link
  • Also dropped by S4 (16 borderline_drops lines in findings.S4.yaml): Infoblox (repeat), Softway Medical, CNIL SAN-2026-016, Neuried, Contabo, DomainFactory, Wellington IT, the NVIDIA/Gentlemen claim, Lithuanian customs, IIHF and Reka, each without a constituency nexus or a transferable behaviour.
  • Not returned by S3 but flagged as possibly missed by earlier fires: Kaspersky's Operation ShadowCloud and AuditTeam OpsAgent posts (2026-11-17/18) and Talos UAT-12643 (2026-11-18), all outside the window; left for the audit's re-sweep.
  • Single-source: USI Lugano (single-source-victim, the victim's communique read through two near-verbatim relays); Mitel OpenScape 4000 (vendor advisory; CERT-FR and BSI restate it).
  • Rotation: 100 standard or candidate sources were excluded from the slices because the previous two fires attempted them (runs.recent_attempts); S1 26, S2 19, S3 14 and S4 8 slice records were all attempted, and belden-psirt and sygnia were extra probes recorded as outside-slice checks, not as attempts.
  • Coverage gaps: baselland-ch (403 on every transport); usi-ch (403, relays used); f5-k-articles (JavaScript shell, CNA records used); perforce-portal (shell, EUVD and press used); belden-psirt (403, reader pool dead); lab52 (listing undated, feed resets); golem article bodies (consent wall, titles only); swisspost-cybersecurity (no dates); senthorus-ch (weekly roundups only).
  • Reader pool: the jina keys answered HTTP 402 almost throughout; no source needed it.
  • Ledger note: S3 rewrote url-liveness.tsv twice (removing lines it had logged in error) while other agents appended, and DR2 reports two portal.perforce.com lines that record a 200 for JavaScript shells; neither is cited.
  • Home-region watch item: Canton Basel-Landschaft (held, expiry 2026-12-03). Re-check search for the next fire: Kanton Basel-Landschaft Cyberangriff Verwaltung Server neu installiert plus the BACS and NCSC.ch hub pages; publish when a source names a vector, behaviour or data taken.
  • Verifier iteration 1 findings declined with reason: the European Commission record stays an update on the ARTEX entry (a new government victim is a development PD-8 names; the section now states the date disagreement); CVE-2026-115732 gets no techniques[] id because no source names a technique the existing mapping lacks; the old PHP entry's main analysis length is left for the audit's compaction pass (this fire's record replaced sentences and added none).
  • Dedup warnings (informational): the vCenter and PHP entries share entities with earlier entries by product; both are distinct findings (a new flaw and a new release) and declare the nearest predecessors in references[].
  • Reverted update: the record on 2026-10-21/php-critical-release-pre-announced-cve-2026-109618-109619 (an improvement that moved its update target to 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36 and fixed its CVE-2026-115560 statements) was reverted with git checkout after verifier iteration 5: touching the 81 KB critical entry put the whole file in verification scope, and the passes kept finding vendor lines (Cisco, Fortinet, GreyNoise start date, two evidence quotes, a Siemens version) that its cited pages had changed since it was last written, defects that predate this fire. Left for the quality audit: that entry still says CVE-2026-115560 is unfixed and names 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 as the targets, while the new PHP entry states the fix; it also needs the VulnCheck note that its exploit covers PHP 7.4.10 to 7.4.33, 8.0.15 to 8.0.30 and 8.1.10 to 8.1.34.
  • Verifier iteration 5 findings declined: the ENISA record for CVE-2026-132825 re-read at the main agent lists three references (Hacker News, the Ruby announcement, the GHSA) and no GitHub reproduction repository, so the Ruby entry states no public proof of concept; Tenable's updated distribution status for the Java4Shell entry (Ubuntu, Red Hat, Debian fixes) belongs to the previous fire's dated section and is left to the audit.
  • Verification: six iterations, none CLEAN; the loop ended on the low-residual early exit after iteration 6 (truth 2, editorial 0, no F1 or F4): both findings were fixed after that pass (the Java4Shell cves[].fixed Cisco qualifier restored, the PHP "left open in October" clause cited to watchTowr) and have not had a further pass, so verification_residual_count is 2. Iteration 1 dropped the F5 BIG-IP entry; iteration 5 led to reverting the October PHP entry's update. The later passes read pages that had changed since the text was written (Zammad 7.2.3, GitLab's Ruby fix, Cisco's updated product table), which is why the loop did not converge on CLEAN.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-11-19
item.description:
• REDCap unauthenticated survey-to-RCE chain exploited and on CISA KEV; upgrade to 16.0.49, 17.3.10 or 17.4.4. Securifera described CVE-2026-90817 on 2026-09-27, a five-step chain in Vanderbilt's REDCap research-data platform that turns a request to a public survey into code execution on the server without authentication, given a valid public survey hash (CVSS 3.1 9.8). Unit 42 reported it exploited on 2026-10-07 to install Monero miners behind a transient web shell, with cron, SSH-key and shell-profile persistence, and CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-18. The fixed builds are 16.0.49 LTS, 17.3.10 LTS and 17.4.4 Standard. →
  • nginx2root: five unauthenticated flaws reach worker RCE, Rapid7 PoC public; update to 1.31.10, 1.30.8, Plus 37.3.1.1. F5 and the nginx project fixed five memory-corruption flaws in the nginx data plane on 2026-11-18, two in HTTP/2 and one each in HTTP/3, the resolver and the mail proxy, which CERT-EU says can lead to unauthenticated code execution with the privileges of the worker process; NCSC-NL scores all five CVSS 4.0 9.2, NCSC.ch and Wiz the two HTTP/2 flaws and Rapid7 CVE-2026-123007. The memory-corruption fixes are in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 and NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1, nginx 1.31.10, 1.30.8 and NGINX Plus 37.3.1.1 and 37.0.9.1 add a fix for one CPU-exhaustion flaw, and NGINX Plus R33 to R36 have no update. Rapid7 published a proof of concept for CVE-2026-123007, CERT-EU reports no exploitation, and NCSC.ch, CERT-EU, CERT.at and NCSC-NL issued warnings; Unit 42 reached pre-authentication code execution through CVE-2026-123633 as the worker user in a lab, on a non-default configuration and with a separate memory leak that F5 has not given a CVE. Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS and Panorama with HTTP/2 enabled as affected, Veeam lists its 13.1 Software and Infrastructure Appliances (fixed through Veeam Updater), Cisco lists Catalyst Center, Identity Services Engine 3.5, Nexus 3000 and 9000 in standalone NX-OS mode, UCS Director and about 20 other products with fixes dated November 2026 to March 2027 or still to be determined, Siemens and Synology list products with fixes pending or none, and Fortinet confirms FortiOS, FortiProxy, FortiMail, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiADC, FortiWeb and FortiSIEM not impacted while 29 product names, FortiAuthenticator among them, remain under investigation. →
  • Cyderes: 'tcherber' VPN toolkit for FortiGate and SonicWall, credential file mixing default and real logins, LDAP sweep. Cyderes' Howler Cell recovered a Go toolkit that wraps OpenConnect for FortiGate and NetExtender for SonicWall, a credential file of more than 500 FortiGate entries mixing default guest, admin and test logins with organisation-specific passwords, and VPN connection logs showing sustained root-level tunnels into multiple victim environments in May and June 2026. Once the tunnel is up the orchestrator maps internal routes and enumerates Active Directory over LDAP, while port scanning, SMB reconnaissance and credential validation are manual tools. Cyderes assesses a Russian-speaking initial access broker and malware-as-a-service seller and names no victim, vulnerability or firmware version. →

TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01REDCap unauthenticated survey-to-RCE chain exploited and on CISA KEV; upgrade to 16.0.49, 17.3.10 or 17.4.4. F5 and the nginx project fixed five memory-corruption flaws in the nginx data plane on 2026-11-18, two in HTTP/2 and one each in HTTP/3, the resolver and the mail proxy, which CERT-EU says can lead to unauthenticated code execution with the privileges of the worker process; NCSC-NL scores all five CVSS 4.0 9.2, NCSC.ch and Wiz the two HTTP/2 flaws and Rapid7 CVE-2026-123007.
