  • Patch vCenter to 9.1.0.0300, 9.0.2.0100 or 8.0 U3k/U2f as applicable (vCenter 7.0 through Broadcom extended support), since there is no workaround, and on any appliance that was network-reachable and unpatched between 29 July and today, check the appliance's own scheduled-task and cron configuration for entries the platform team did not create, and its egress records for outbound SSH sessions from the appliance itself.
    FindingCVE-2026-59309 +4→
  • On the ESX hosts of any vCenter estate that was exposed or compromised, install the build that fixes CVE-2026-41709 and review administrator activity from vCenter task and event records and from syslog forwarded off the host, because Broadcom says the flaw lets an administrator act without being logged and CrowdStrike reports it used as a zero-day.
    FindingCVE-2026-59309 +4→
  • Inventory Joomla sites for the Balbooa Gridbox page builder and update every one to 2.20.5.0, which also closes an unauthenticated file deletion and three further flaws fixed on 2026-11-04 and, from 2.20.4.2, two unauthenticated SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 and CVE-2026-102789, and the unauthenticated blind SQL injection in the front-end blog author parameter fixed in 2.20.3.1, present in every earlier build, 2.20.3 and 2.20.2.3 included. Anything below 2.20.2 is also exposed to the exploited follow-up batch, which 2.20.1 does not close.
    FindingCVE-2026-61425 +11→
  • On any site that ran Gridbox 2.20.1 or earlier while internet-reachable, review the Super User list and administrator-group members, remove accounts that entered an admin group through self-registration rather than an explicit administrative action, and review template files and the web root for changes, with particular attention to files written since 20 July, when the cookie bypass was disclosed.
    FindingCVE-2026-61425 +11→
  • Upgrade every Belden NetModule NRSW router to 5.0.0.105, and where that is not yet possible disable its web interface after confirming SSH access, with the CLI settings http.status=0 and https.status=0; patch macmon 7.x from the service portal and move macmon 6.x to 7.x, and keep the web interfaces of both off networks that are not trusted.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • Take the management interface of every PA-Series and VM-Series firewall and Panorama off the internet now by restricting it to a jump box or trusted internal addresses, because Palo Alto reports active exploitation against internet-exposed management interfaces, and install the hotfix PAN-SA-2026-0015 lists for your maintenance release (12.2.4-h3; 12.1.4-h15, 12.1.7-h15, 12.1.10-h6; 11.2.4-h25, 11.2.7-h25, 11.2.10-h19, 11.2.13-h6, 11.2.16-h3; 11.1.4-h40, 11.1.6-h42, 11.1.7-h14, 11.1.10-h38, 11.1.13-h18, 11.1.16-h6; 10.2.7-h41, 10.2.10-h45, 10.2.13-h29, 10.2.16-h14, 10.2.18-h15), which includes the PHP2Shell fix and fixes the kernel flaw as well.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +2→
  • Rotate the directory bind account, HA replication keys, certificate private keys and device authentication keys of every PAN-OS firewall and Panorama that was reachable from the internet while unpatched and shows a PHP web shell or a tunnel, because the chain Dream Research recovered harvested exactly those from rooted firewalls, and the hotfix does not remove a web shell or tunnel already in place.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +2→
  • Deploy the 2026-10-13 cumulative update for each release (KB5127648 for Windows 11 24H2, 25H2 and 26H2, KB5127646 for Windows 11 26H1, KB5126657 for Windows 10 21H2 and 22H2, KB5126655 for Server 2022, KB5126646 for Server 2025, and the others listed in the CVE record) to every Windows endpoint and server, starting with the systems whose users open mail and chat attachments or download files; Rapid7 says Windows Server 2012 receives no patch; confirm that Microsoft Edge is at 154.0.4258.62 or later, which Microsoft added to the fix list on 2026-10-26.
    FindingCVE-2026-96951→
  • On every internet-facing Linux server and every XenServer or XCP-ng host with its Workload Balancing and Conversion Manager appliances, install the vendor's fixed kernel or firmware and reboot, then confirm the running version.
    FindingCVE-2026-98432→
  • On Veeam estates, run Veeam Updater on the appliances, install the private fix for the Linux helper appliances of Windows-based Backup & Replication and of Recovery Orchestrator 13.1, redeploy virtual labs and helper appliances that stay deployed and replace recovery media made before the update.
    FindingCVE-2026-98432→
  • On hosts that cannot reboot yet, drop IPv4 TCP packets that carry IP options ahead of the TCP stack as CIQ, AWS and Vates describe, after testing on one non-production host because it also drops legitimate option-bearing traffic; disabling MPTCP alone does not close the path.
    FindingCVE-2026-98432→
  • Update every non-browser TLS client that keeps its own CA bundle or does not check revocation to a fixed version: standalone Java runtimes, including those already updated on 2026-10-21, to the update of Oracle's Security Alert CVE-2026-114820 or OpenJDK (Oracle Database Server, Autonomous Health Framework and OPatch installations too), Python 3.15.2, 3.14.10, 3.13.18, 3.12.16 or 3.11.18 together with pip 26.2.2 or later, Go 1.27.3 or 1.26.10, self-managed GitLab to a fixed patch release together with GitLab Runner 19.5.1, and SonicWall Gen7 firewalls with Client DPI-SSL enabled to SonicOS 7.3.4-7015 or later and Gen8 to 8.2.3-8015 or later; then confirm with curl against the incident tracker's test host that the client rejects the certificate; on managed Macs update to macOS 27.2.1, 26.7.3 or 15.8.3, or where that is not possible remove emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from /etc/ssl/cert.pem as Apple describes (AAA Certificate Services is optional and can stop tools that read only that file from verifying some unaffected sites).
    FindingCVE-2026-91403 +3→
  • Replace, by hand where the ACME client does not support ACME Renewal Information, every TLS certificate your organisation holds that chains to emSign ECC Root CA - G3 or to another of the seven certificates Microsoft removed from the Windows and Edge trust lists, or that was issued by one of the eight RSA G2B and G2C issuing CAs eMudhra revoked on 2026-11-07, because Chrome's removal of the G3 root was due on 2026-10-27 and the Windows change takes effect when the trust-list update reaches a device; deliver the updated Disallowed Certificate Trust List and the trust-list changes Microsoft describes, including its out-of-band update of 2026-10-26, to Windows devices that do not receive automatic certificate-trust updates; do not renew or reissue under emSign Root CA - G1 after 2026-11-16, because Chrome 153 and higher will not trust by default a certificate under it whose earliest SCT is later, and Windows, Edge and WebView2 stop trusting the remaining eMudhra roots on 2026-11-16 as Microsoft's update of 2026-11-10 describes.
    FindingCVE-2026-91403 +3→
  • Apply Cisco's remediation now for the products its eMudhra advisory (version 1.11) lists with a fix or a procedure available: the CA-trust distrust guide for IOS XE and the guidance for Secure Firewall ASA, FTD and FMC, Secure Email Gateway and Secure Email and Web Manager (run the updatenow command where updates are manual), Duo Access Gateway 3.2.0, Duo Network Gateway 3.4.1, Duo Agentic Authorization Connector 1.0.1 and ThousandEyes Enterprise Agent (Application-hosting Agent 5.2.2).
    FindingCVE-2026-91403 +3→
  • Run an organisation-scoped GitHub code search in every organisation your teams and suppliers administer for workflow files under .github/workflows that present themselves as a security audit, a security check or an Actions security workflow and were added since 2026-08-31; any hit means assume breach: revoke the credential that committed it, rotate every secret found anywhere in the repository's git history, not only the configured Actions secrets, and check the crontab of every developer machine and self-hosted runner that opened or ran the repository since 2026-10-14 for a five-minute job that runs a remote script.
    FindingGhostAction: fake security workflows now harvest…→
  • Update every on-premise Adobe Campaign Classic v7 server, and the on-premise components of any hybrid deployment, to build 9403; build 9402 is affected by APSB26-162, including a SQL injection that needs no privileges, build 9401 fixes only APSB26-134's three flaws, and an Adobe-hosted instance that still reports 9401 is not evidence of exposure.
    FindingCVE-2026-82004 +20→
Verification & coverage notes2 runs

2026-11-01T1312Z-audit · audit · Opus 5.5 · window 168 h · 0 entries published

Scope and outcome

Scheduled weekly audit of 2026-10-25T13:08Z to 2026-11-01T13:12Z (anchor: the 2026-10-25 audit, the last with re-sweeps). Fifty-four entries with activity from the week's seven intel fires were truth-checked whole in six passes: 30 clean, 22 with imprecisions, 2 with factual errors. The re-sweeps found no gap that needed a new entry; six developments on covered findings were added as records. Twenty-four entries carry one record each from this fire (7 updates, 13 corrections, 4 improvements; 7 internal). Report: docs/audits/2026-11-01-quality-audit.md.

Verification & coverage notes

  • Claims: an open partial claim from cleanup wave 05 (2026-10-21T1147Z-audit, partial 2026-10-21T11:47:42Z wave=05) still stands on main; the scheduled audit ignores a partial claim (Phase 0 step 2), and it is more than 48 h old.
  • Budget: 13 of 20 spawns (six truth passes, G1 to G3, four verifier passes), 6,885,964 sub-agent tokens: 4,748,994 before the verifier loop and 2,136,970 in it (work/2026-11-01T1312Z-audit/budget.tsv).
  • Verification: four passes over this fire's changed claims, the run record and the report. Iterations 1 and 2 returned NEEDS_FIXES (7 and 3 truth findings), all remediated; iteration 3 returned CLEAN; iteration 4, the confirmation pass over all 242 claims, found no truth defect and two editorial ones (two cves[].affected strings not brought in line with this fire's own fixed-build additions), both applied. Decision rule 5 (truth plus editorial at most 2, no F1 or F4) publishes on that early exit; the residual is 2, the two editorial findings, which were applied after the pass and are unverified by a further pass. The pre-existing advisories left for the next truth pass are the Dream citation dates on the CVE-2026-46300 entry.
  • Truth passes: 54 entries in six batches, 1,651 ledger claims, every claim answered (12 unreadable in TA, mostly NetScaler's Tech Zone post that returns 403 on every transport). Verdicts: 30 clean, 22 imprecision, 2 factual error.
  • Records: 24 entries carry one record each (7 update, 13 correction, 4 improvement; 7 internal). The six re-sweep developments are records on covered entries; no new entry was needed.
  • KEV: ten additions since 2026-10-25, all covered (work/2026-11-01T1312Z-audit/kev-window.txt); no COVERED-STALE or RANSOMWARE row.
  • Backlog: ARX Group SA held to 2026-11-07; G2 found no victim, client or press confirmation.
  • borderline-drop: Adobe Campaign Classic APSB26-162 as a new entry: published instead as an update on the 2026-10-02 entry, whose fixed build it supersedes.
  • borderline-drop: ESET APT Activity Report Q2-Q3 2026, Talos VOLTA and NIK C2, Check Point Yoba, Elastic wesp.sys, Symantec AI relays, Group-IB MadApe, Microsoft's DPRK AI staging, Kaspersky cloud isolation, the MEP letter on ad-delivered spyware, Apple's notification wave, Zimperium's Coruna and DarkSword counts (G3): no constituency decision.
  • borderline-drop: Contact Form 7 6.2.4, Sophos UTM CVE-2026-118633, TeamViewer TV-2026-1011, the Drupal contrib wave of 2026-10-28, Splunk, Mitel, Jenkins, EPICS, Adobe Connect, LXD, Thales Sentinel, Teltonika, vsftpd, TightVNC, WolfVision, Grafana, the Synology SA-26:15 and Fortinet FG-IR-26-187 notices for the covered Brotli flaw (G1): unexploited, regular cycle, no constituency exposure, or a vendor notice that adds no decision to the covered entry.
  • borderline-drop: Sophos UTM CVE-2026-118633 (Sophos advisory 2026-10-28, pre-auth root RCE, all versions, end of life, manual patch): no exploitation or proof of concept reported, it needs the email proxy with scanning enabled and minutes of sustained racing (not a single-request path), EPSS 0.006, and the product is end of life with a manual patch as the only fix; verifier iteration 1 raised it as a missed angle (F10, low confidence) and the audit keeps the drop, to be reopened on an exploitation report.
  • borderline-drop: Camping.Care supplier-side statement (a Dutch campsite's notice of 2026-10-23, G2): it predates the window and adds only that the platform operator told campsites data was presumably taken, which the covered entry's incident framing already carries.
  • borderline-drop: SolNet, SIHF, SoftwareOne, Leipzig University, Fehmarnbelt FLC, Verrières-en-Forez, the Federal Council alerting dispatch, the e-evidence transitional rule, the Geneva e-voting step, the BACS week-43 WhatsApp wave, EFK report on ZEMIS (G2): below the incident floor or no defender consequence.
  • Declined truth-pass findings, with reasons in the report: Adobe Commerce Events for CVE-2026-48356, the MDaemon KEV ransomware flag (WinRAR vector), the WS_FTP CVE-2026-90867 mitigation (CVE record API only), the Gridbox high (low-confidence F16), T1611 on CVE-2026-46300, Publica's early volume statement.
  • Source health: sans-isc content scope set; ico-uk (timeouts), ssd-disclosure (transient) and connectwise-trust-center (flapping) investigated and left as they are; no webfetch-only record.
  • Reader pool (context): 6 of 10 jina keys live, balance about 46.8 M; G3 saw extract fall through to the reader seven times on Dark Reading.
  • ATT&CK pin: up to date (local v20.0 == upstream v20.0).
  • Tool change: tools/check_run.py now appends every run-scope gate output to work/<run-id>/gate.log; exercised on this fire's gate runs.
  • Coverage gaps: sygnia (blocked on every transport), cyberscoop and technadu feeds (10 items, 2026-10-25 to 10-27 not listed), F5 K000163821 and the per-product Broadcom advisories (JS shell or login), apa-ots (feed about 3 h deep), risikomonitor.ch (no DNS from the container).

2026-11-01T0256Z-intel · Sonnet 5.5 · window 26 h · 1 entry published

Verification & coverage notes

  • Window: standard class, gap 24.0 h to 2026-10-31T0256Z-intel, window 26 h. The window is a Saturday and a Sunday: every authority and trade feed in the slices has its newest item on 2026-10-30 or earlier (NCSC.ch security hub 2026-10-30T14:22Z, BACS pages 2026-10-27 and older, NCSC-NL, BSI, CERT-EU, CERT.at, CERT-PL, ENISA, NCSC-UK, CISA, Inside IT, Netzwoche). A thin window is the healthy outcome here, not a miss.
  • KEV sweep: kev_window_diff.py found no CISA KEV additions inside the window, and S1's own read of catalog 2026.10.30 agrees (the newest additions, the two Ivanti flaws of 2026-10-30, are covered). No KEV row needs a disposition.
  • Backlog: the ARX Group SA / Aurora row stays held. S4 re-checked on 2026-11-01 (DE, FR, IT and EN searches; Inside IT through 2026-10-30; the tio.ch, SRF, RTS, Netzwoche, ICTjournal and Blick listings; the arx.ing homepage) and found no statement from ARX, SBB, ASTRA or Swiss press; Ransomware.live still shows the bare claim with no press link. The row's expiry stays 2026-11-07, struck if the condition is unmet.
  • Dispositions (PD-8): the PAN-OS naming and the Unit 42 verification are an update on 2026-10-22/pan-os-panorama-php2shell-mgmt-interface-no-fixed-release; the Fragnesia entry carried the same stale "one unnamed vendor" statement and takes an improvement that names the vendor without re-floating it; the PHP2Shell main entry takes an update that names the vendor and adds GreyNoise's sensor data and Hunt.io's captures (follow-up FU1, spawned on the verifier's missed-angle finding). GTIG and Mandiant's incident-response report is an update on the ARTEX entry; Microsoft's trust-list removal, Cisco's advisory v1.5 and GitLab's release are an update on the eMudhra entry.
  • Recency (PD-7): the PAN-OS update rests on Dream Research (2026-10-29) and Unit 42 (2026-10-29), and the eMudhra update on Microsoft (2026-10-26), GitLab (2026-10-29), Python (2026-10-26) and Cisco v1.5 (2026-10-30), all dated before the 26 h horizon of 2026-10-31T00:56Z and none carried by the previous fire. They are admitted as first coverage from rotational sources' lookback (Dream through S3, GitLab through S1) and as changelog records on covered entries that predate them, each moving what a reader does (the post-patch compromise check and the Windows trust-list removal). The GreyNoise tracker (2026-11-01) and Hunt.io (2026-10-28, revised 2026-10-30) additions to the PHP2Shell entry come from the FU1 follow-up. The GTIG report is in window.
  • Sourcing: the Vaud entry is single-source-victim; RTS repeats the canton's release and adds a pupil suspicion without a further named source, which the entry attributes to RTS. The PAN-OS entry moves from single-source to multi-source (Dream Research and Unit 42 describe the chain; the two worked together, so credibility stays 2 and the actor claim rests on Dream's relay of Unit 42's CL-UNK-1280 designation). Hunt.io's PAN-OS rooting sentence relays Dream and Unit 42 and is not an independent vantage.
  • Source inconsistencies carried: GTIG's introduction lists ARTEX, Hexstrike and CAIRN while its observations list ARTEX, PentAGI and CAIRN (sourcing note of the ARTEX entry). Dream says the PAN-OS management web server also fronts the GlobalProtect portal, while Palo Alto's advisory says GlobalProtect is not affected; the entry states both, attributed (see the Contradiction line). Dream's page title counts 25 servers where earlier text counted 24 (24 batch-rooted firewalls plus the internal management server).
  • Contradiction: Dream says the PAN-OS management web server also fronts the GlobalProtect portal; Palo Alto's advisory says GlobalProtect is not affected. The PAN-OS entry states both, attributed. Hunt.io says PAN-OS runs one uniform PHP 8.0.30 build and that the exploit reliably roots it; Dream lists PHP 7.4.33 on PAN-OS 11.1 and 24 rooted of 240 targeted. The entries carry Dream's version and count only.
  • borderline-drop: ESET APT Activity Report Q2 to Q3 2026: no Swiss or public-sector finding beyond the MDaemon item already covered.
  • borderline-drop: Talos VOLTA and NIK C2 (AI-integrated implants): effort-displacement novelty with no decision change; NIK C2 is also outside the window.
  • borderline-drop: Kaspersky NetamLoader: one Asian victim, no attribution, no constituency nexus.
  • borderline-drop: Check Point Yoba: XMRig miner payload through fake AI-app repositories, no nexus.
  • borderline-drop: Huntress camera-management-software intrusion: vendor and initial access unknown, low confidence.
  • borderline-drop: Binance USD 6.36 billion theft: passes only the global-scale clause, no Swiss nexus, and the vector is one clause (a DevOps laptop and a service container) with no transferable technique detail.
  • borderline-drop: Chainalysis intrusion: method undisclosed, no Swiss customer named (incident floor).
  • borderline-drop: Northflank environment-variable exposure: no Swiss or public-sector nexus.
  • borderline-drop: Node2Shell vendor-list additions (Cisco still investigating, Prisma Cloud Transporter Client 0.2.9, Stormshield Management Center 3.9.4): marginal product-list additions on a covered entry.
  • borderline-drop: Android SMS of Death (CVE-2026-58882): denial of service only, and the CVE id comes from BleepingComputer alone with no NVD or EUVD record on 2026-11-01.
  • borderline-drop: TeamViewer TV-2026-1011 (CVE-2026-111585 and two more, fixed in 15.83): a user-interaction flaw that needs the viewer to connect to a hostile host, no exploitation known, patchable in the normal cycle; the sources date from 2026-10-28 to 2026-10-30.
  • borderline-drop: Sophos GOLD OGRE/Aur0ra AI-agent ransomware and Microsoft's North Korean AI-adoption post: no constituency decision.
  • borderline-drop: SIHF portal credential-abuse breach, Holcim leak-site claim, SALEG and INED claims, Oberspreewald-Lausitz district administration: no Swiss public-sector nexus or no victim confirmation.
  • Carry-forward for the next fire (S1): Cisco's advance notice of 2026-10-28 says advisories for ISE, UCS Central and Unified CM publish on 2026-11-04.
  • Candidate source added: vd-ch-press-releases (primary for cantonal disclosures; both S2 and S4 proposed it). Proposed and not added, to keep to about one per run: letemps-cyber, ms-trusted-root-program, remedio-research, php.events.greynoise.io (GreyNoise's per-flaw event tracker, worth a per-fire check while a flaw is in KEV). Recipe findings are in the sources_changed notes: mandiant-gtig (the FeedBurner feed lags and missed the 2026-10-31 post), enisa-euvd, lab52, swissinfo-ger, phorion.
  • Coverage gaps: connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport); ox-security (article bodies 403); lab52 (feed SSL EOF, listing read through the reader, nothing in horizon); Tamedia pages (tagesanzeiger.ch, 24heures.ch) fall to the metered reader or return page chrome.
  • Watchlist: not configured (product, supplier and standing-interest lists empty).
  • Source-health repairs of this fire (UNSOLVED list): sans-isc now reads its feed (fetch_method rss, health_cmd feed), frenchbreaches gets a feed health_cmd, vd-ch-press-releases is content_scope: general-news; ico-uk stays flagged needs-demote because the direct sitemap read, extract and WebFetch all timed out today, a transport timeout that never demotes (the recipe worked on 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-27).
  • Verifier iteration 1 (NEEDS_FIXES, 23 findings) was remediated before iteration 2; its follow-up research FU1 ran on the missed-angle finding. The run's own verification block carries the outcomes.
  • Verification: eight iterations, the cap. Iteration 1 returned NEEDS_FIXES with 23 findings and iteration 5 a first CLEAN (three advisories left); the confirmation pass, iteration 6, returned NEEDS_FIXES (two truth findings, both fixed), and iterations 7 and 8 returned NEEDS_FIXES on small wording, date and citation defects. The loop ended at the cap and publishes under the fail-open rule with verification_residual_count 3, the truth and editorial findings of iteration 8. Those three (a Threat ID range on the PAN-OS entry, an OpenJDK citation date on the eMudhra entry, a "first documented code execution" claim on the PHP2Shell entry) were corrected after the last pass and are not re-verified; the next quality audit should give those three entries an independent read.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-31
item.description:
• WS_FTP Server: unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 admin-credential leak, five more critical flaws; fix 2025.0.4, 2024.0.7. Progress's bulletin, as listed by heise, covers fifteen WS_FTP Server flaws on Windows, six of them critical: CVE-2026-84295, an improper-authentication flaw that could let an unauthenticated remote attacker reach administrative credentials (CVSS 3.1 10.0), and five command-injection, path-traversal and missing-authorization flaws (CVE-2026-90868 at 9.9, CVE-2026-90866, CVE-2026-90864 and CVE-2026-90863 at 9.1, CVE-2026-90865 at 9.0), four of which NCSC Switzerland describes as a route from the exposed administrator credentials to full server compromise. Builds before 2024.0.7 and 2025.0.4 are affected, and CSIRT Italia says Progress will issue no patch for unsupported versions. NCSC Switzerland lists exploitation as unknown and no source reports it; CISA's catalog holds no 2026 WS_FTP flaw, though a 2023 flaw in the same product is listed with known ransomware use. →
  • Microsoft: Teams help-desk vishing into Quick Assist ended in AD CS certificates for privileged accounts and a DC. Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes two human-operated intrusions, not attributed to any actor, in which an external Teams contact impersonating help-desk staff got a user to open Quick Assist, after which the operator staged a portable runtime and used Active Directory Certificate Services to reach privileged identities: a template open to ESC1 issued certificates for privileged accounts and DCSync followed within seconds, and in the second case PetitPotam was relayed to AD CS Web Enrollment (ESC8) for a certificate for a domain controller account. An issued certificate stays valid after a password reset or a reimage of the first workstation, and in the first case one privileged account excluded from automated containment stayed usable and was used to copy data to an external SFTP destination. →
  • Cursor marketplace served a trojanised Claude Code extension for 11 hours; uninstalling leaves the SSH backdoor. Between about 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29 the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace served a modified copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for macOS and Windows, that appends an attacker's SSH key to authorized_keys, tries to enable SSH and open a reverse tunnel, and installs persistence that outlives the extension; coding errors made the SSH step fail on most standard-user hosts, so Cursor says the attacker could not log in there. Cursor's report of 2026-11-13 says the chain began with an access key it had issued to its vendor Fireworks AI, exposed by Fireworks, which gave the attacker a storage bucket of coding-agent traces holding some unredacted credentials, and that a stolen credential from the exposed data let the attacker write the extension straight onto the marketplace cache; Cursor says this was not a vulnerability in Anthropic's product. →

Teams help-desk impersonation to domain-controller identity: Microsoft traces two intrusions from a Quick Assist session to AD CS ESC1 certificates with DCSync, and to PetitPotam relayed to ESC8 Web Enrollment

Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes two human-operated intrusions, not attributed to any threat actor, that began with an external Teams contact (across the broader activity Microsoft saw organisation-themed tenant names and support-style display names) who persuaded a user to open Quick Assist and read out the connection code; the activity did not exploit a Teams vulnerability. In the session the operator placed an archive in Downloads, extracted it into a newly created KB-prefixed folder under the user profile and started the payload with a portable Python, JavaScript or Java runtime, which ran host and network discovery and assessed AD CS (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30).

In the first case a certificate template open to ESC1, where the requester supplies the identity, produced certificates for three privileged accounts, and about 90 minutes later for eight more after a second wave against 16 users; DCSync began within seconds of obtaining one privileged certificate. Defender's automated disruption blocked more than 1,000 SMB attempts, but a privileged account excluded from automated response stayed usable, reached a file server and ran a renamed Rclone that copied a share to an external SFTP destination (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30). In the second case the operator used PetitPotam to make a domain controller authenticate to the attacker's host, relayed that NTLM authentication to an AD CS Web Enrollment endpoint, obtained a certificate from the Domain Controller template and used it for PKINIT to get a ticket-granting ticket for the controller's account; Defender raised ESC8 alerts and the customer isolated the workstation (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30).

Exposure
A forest with an enterprise CA whose authentication-capable templates accept requester-supplied identity with broad enrollment rights (ESC1), or whose Web Enrollment or Certificate Enrollment Web Service endpoints lack HTTPS and Extended Protection (ESC8), where Teams accepts external chats and calls and users can start Quick Assist; Defender for Identity's AD CS posture assessments, or an inventory of /certsrv endpoints and template permissions, shows the first two (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30).
Detection
New external Teams contacts from help-desk-themed tenants; in process telemetry, a portable runtime started from a freshly created KB-prefixed folder under the user profile after a remote-support session; in CA records, certificate requests and issuances correlated by requester, subject alternative name and template with the first authentication using the certificate; and a domain controller account authenticating to Web Enrollment from a device that is not that controller, which Microsoft calls a strong pivot (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30). After containment, revoke the unauthorized certificates and assess issued Kerberos tickets separately; a password reset and a reimage of the first workstation leave both in place.

Triage: a help-desk Quick Assist session is routine; what separates this one is an external-tenant initiator with no matching ticket and an interpreter runtime launched from a newly created user-writable folder rather than a managed install path.

Defender takeaway
Require HTTPS and Extended Protection on every enrollment web endpoint, drop the ones nobody needs, review authentication-capable templates and require approval where enrollment is broad, and enable the Certification Services audit subcategory and CA audit filter; limit Teams external access and restrict remote-support tools to approved ones. Treat a containment exclusion as an incident decision with a manual compensating step, because in the first case the one excluded privileged account was the route to the file server (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30).

Cursor marketplace: a tampered Claude Code extension (versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313) planted an SSH key, a reverse tunnel and persistence for about eleven hours on 2026-10-29; uninstalling it does not remove the persistence

Between about 2:27am PT and 1:35pm PT on 2026-10-29 (09:27 to 20:35 UTC) a maliciously modified copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for macOS and Windows, was served from the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace; Cursor removed it, rebuilt the marketplace, rotated its keys and had the attacker's server taken offline (Cursor, 2026-10-29). Anthropic told Microsoft its systems were not compromised and that it did not build the package, and Microsoft confirms the packages were never published to the Visual Studio Marketplace or npm (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30). Cursor's report of 2026-11-13 says the attacker wrote the copies onto the marketplace cache with a credential taken through a key exposed at its vendor Fireworks, and that at most 5,000 users potentially received the build (Cursor, 2026-11-13).

The injected loader runs when the extension module loads (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30). It reports host and user data (hostname, username, operating system, directories, Git email, environment-variable names and public IP address), appends an attacker-controlled SSH public key to authorized_keys, tries to enable the local SSH service and open a reverse SSH tunnel, and installs persistence outside the extension: a LaunchAgent on macOS, and on Windows a scheduled task that asks to run as SYSTEM with a Startup-folder fallback, with background scripts retrying the tunnel about every 60 seconds (Cursor, 2026-10-29). Microsoft's analysis adds a user crontab entry for Linux (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30). Because of coding errors, enabling SSH fails unless Cursor was started with administrator privileges, so on most hosts the attacker could not log in through the tunnel, but the key, persistence and host report remained (Cursor, 2026-10-29).

Exposure
Any macOS or Windows host on which Cursor installed or auto-updated Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 inside the window; the code also carries Linux routines though Cursor names only macOS and Windows packages (heise online, 2026-10-30). Extension-install telemetry shows the version. NCSC Switzerland's post of 2026-10-30 places the extension on Open VSX (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-30); Cursor says Open VSX never had it (Cursor, 2026-11-13). Cursor says coding-agent traces from sessions outside Privacy Mode were exposed for fewer than 0.05% of users, all notified, so a user with no notice was not among them (Cursor, 2026-11-13).
Detection
In process-creation telemetry, an editor's extension host starting ssh or autossh with remote port forwarding and no command; in file-write telemetry, an editor process modifying authorized_keys; and, shortly after an extension update, a new LaunchAgent, scheduled task, Startup-folder script or @reboot crontab entry named after system-monitoring components. Phorion advises matching the attacker key's fingerprint rather than the comment string it carries (Phorion, 2026-10-30). Removing the extension does not remove the persistence scripts, which keep running (Cursor, 2026-10-29).

Triage: a running SSH process is not proof the attacker got in, since both ends must allow the connection (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30); administrators run tunnels too, and what separates this one is an editor extension as the parent process and persistence written to user-writable locations rather than a managed service.

Defender takeaway
Treat a host that ran either version as backdoored whether or not the tunnel connected: remove the key, the persistence and the tunnel processes, rebuild where compromise cannot be excluded, and rotate credentials reachable from it. heise reports a cleaned release, with 2.1.314 as the minimum to install (heise online, 2026-10-30).

CVE-2026-84295, Progress WS_FTP Server: an unauthenticated remote authentication flaw can expose administrative credentials (CVSS 10.0), with two more unauthenticated flaws, fixed in 2025.0.4 and 2024.0.7; no exploitation found

Progress, as CNA, published CVE-2026-84295 on 2026-10-29: improper authentication in WS_FTP Server on Windows that "could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to access sensitive information, including administrative credentials"; its CVSS 3.1 vector is network, low complexity, no privileges and no user interaction, scored 10.0, and the record names no component or endpoint (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-29). Two further flaws carry an unauthenticated vector with high attack complexity: CVE-2026-90865, an OS command injection that could allow command execution with elevated privileges under certain configurations (9.0) (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-29), and CVE-2026-90867, improper access control in the Web Admin console that could expose administrative functionality to remote authentication attempts (8.1) (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-29). CSIRT Italia counts 6 critical and 3 high flaws in the release, of types including authentication bypass, remote code execution and arbitrary file read and write (CSIRT Italia, 2026-10-30).

The record for CVE-2026-84295 names versions before 2024.0.6 and 2025.0.3 as affected (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-29), and the records for the other two name versions before 2024.0.7 and 2025.0.4 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-29), so 2024.0.7 or 2025.0.4 is the build to reach. CSIRT Italia lists 2025.0.3 (10.0.3) and 2024.0.6 (9.0.6) and earlier as affected and says that for unsupported versions the vendor will not release a workaround or patch (translated from Italian) (CSIRT Italia, 2026-10-30). No source reports exploitation: CISA's catalog holds no 2026 WS_FTP flaw, although CVE-2023-40044 in the same product has been listed since 2023-10-05 with known ransomware use (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-10-30).

Progress's bulletin, as listed by heise, carries fifteen CVEs, six of them critical (heise online, 2026-11-02). Besides the three above: CVE-2026-90868, an OS command injection that could allow arbitrary command execution under certain configurations (9.9) (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29); CVE-2026-90866, a path traversal by a delegated Host Administrator, potentially enabling remote code execution (9.1) (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29); CVE-2026-90864, a path traversal that lets a delegated Host Administrator reach data beyond their permitted scope (9.1) (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29); and CVE-2026-90863, missing authorization in the administrative interface (9.1) (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29). NCSC Switzerland describes the exposed administrator credentials as the start of a chain: command injection under certain configurations (CVE-2026-90868, CVE-2026-90865) or a scope escape (CVE-2026-90863, CVE-2026-90866) leads to a complete compromise of the server, and it lists exploitation as unknown (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-02). Builds 2024.0.7 and 2025.0.4 have been available since 2026-10-01 (heise online, 2026-11-02).

Exposure
Any WS_FTP Server on Windows below 2024.0.7 or 2025.0.4; CSIRT Italia describes it as a secure file-transfer server used within organisations and with external partners, so instances reachable from partner or public networks come first (CSIRT Italia, 2026-10-30). The records name no component for the authentication flaw, so no configuration is known to make an instance safe.
Detection
No source publishes an indicator. For an instance that was reachable before the fix, the records to review are the web-server logs of the Web Admin console and the file-transfer server's own logons for administrator access from unfamiliar addresses, and process creation by the service or its web worker, since CVE-2026-90865 is command execution (an inference from the described flaw).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade to 2024.0.7 or 2025.0.4, partner-facing instances first, and rotate the administrator credentials afterwards, because the upgrade does not change credentials an attacker already read; take an instance on an unsupported branch off the network or migrate it.

CVE-2026-98432, Linux kernel IPv4 TCP: a use-after-free in connection setup, present since 4.4, has an Anthropic-built remote root exploit against MPTCP listeners that CloudLinux could not reproduce; Citrix XenServer, XCP-ng, MikroTik, Red Hat, Debian, CIQ, Amazon Linux, Ubuntu's generic kernels for 22.04 to 26.10 and Sophos have fixes, Ubuntu 20.04 and older and some HWE, FIPS, NVIDIA and Azure variant kernels are in progress and WatchGuard and Fortinet have none for their products (CVSS 9.8)

The Linux kernel CVE team published CVE-2026-98432 on 2026-10-15; the kernel.org CNA scores it 9.8 while upstream rates it 8.1 with high attack complexity (CIQ, 2026-10-30). It is a use-after-free in the IPv4 TCP connection setup path, introduced in Linux 4.4 and fixed upstream in 6.12.113, 6.18.56, 7.2.10 and 7.3-rc7 (Linux kernel CVE team, 2026-10-15). An unauthenticated peer starts it by sending TCP SYN packets that carry IPv4 options, and a retransmitted SYN can then touch the freed option memory (CIQ, 2026-10-30).

Anthropic wrote on 2026-10-27 that Claude produced an exploit that gives a remote attacker root on a Linux server with a multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener (Anthropic, 2026-10-27), but CloudLinux's kernel team could not reproduce the claim (CloudLinux, 2026-11-02). Akamai is not aware of a public working exploit and says disabling MPTCP alone does not prevent exploitation (Akamai, 2026-11-02), whereas Vates, XCP-ng and WatchGuard say a public exploit exists or circulates (XCP-ng, 2026-11-04; Vates, 2026-11-04; WatchGuard, 2026-11-03). No source reports attacks, and NCSC-NL judges large-scale abuse unlikely given the exploit's complexity (NCSC-NL, 2026-10-30).

Debian, Red Hat, CIQ and AWS have fixed kernels (Debian Security Tracker, 2026-11-03; Red Hat, 2026-11-03; CIQ, 2026-11-01; AWS, 2026-11-02), and Ubuntu's tracker, last updated 2026-11-10, lists 22.04 LTS to 26.10 as fixed (linux 5.15.0-203.213, 6.8.0-149.149, 7.0.0-43.43 and 7.3.0-10.10) while 20.04, 18.04 and 16.04 are still in progress (Canonical, 2026-11-10). Citrix has fixed its XenServer appliances (Citrix, 2026-11-03). XCP-ng released a kernel fix (XCP-ng, 2026-11-04), MikroTik's RouterOS 7.25.1 and 7.24.6 changelogs list the CVE (MikroTik, 2026-11-02; MikroTik, 2026-10-30), Sophos released Sophos Firewall hotfix HF110626.1 on 2026-11-06 and SD-RED firmware 3.0.012 on 2026-11-05 (Sophos, 2026-11-06), and Veeam's KB4966 says its Software and Infrastructure Appliances, workers, helper appliances and recovery media include an affected kernel, fixed through Veeam Updater or a private fix (Veeam, 2026-11-10). WatchGuard lists Fireware OS, AP and Dimension as potentially affected with no fix (WatchGuard, 2026-11-03); Fortinet names no fixed build but added an IPS virtual patch in FMWP database update 26.113 on 2026-11-07 (Fortinet, 2026-11-07).

Exposure
A Linux host on a kernel below the fixed builds that accepts IPv4 TCP connections from an attacker; the demonstrated exploit needs an MPTCP listener, which sudo ss -M -l -n -p -e lists and which Go programs enable on Linux listen sockets by default since Go 1.24 unless the multipathtcp GODEBUG setting or a per-socket option overrides it (Akamai, 2026-11-02; Go team, 2026-10-29). CIQ's testing found that setting net.mptcp.enabled to 0 leaves the plain-TCP path reachable (CIQ, 2026-10-30), and Akamai reports a similar flaw when request-socket migration is on (Akamai, 2026-11-02).
Detection
No source publishes an indicator. Because the trigger is a SYN packet with IP options (CIQ, 2026-10-30) and a lost race only fails the handshake, so the attacker can retry (Anthropic, 2026-10-27), repeated option-bearing SYNs from one source toward a listener in firewall or flow telemetry are the pattern the mechanism implies.
Defender takeaway
Install the distribution kernel and reboot as soon as it ships and confirm the running version afterwards; Ubuntu 20.04 and older and some variant kernels were not out on 2026-11-10. Until then, drop IPv4 TCP packets whose header carries IP options before the TCP stack sees them, tested first on one non-production host because it also drops legitimate option-bearing traffic; disabling MPTCP alone does not remove the path (CIQ, 2026-10-30).

CVE-2026-118539, Drupal Commerce Core: an access bypass in routes and entity fields is exploited against online stores, fixed in 3.3.13 and 8.x-2.41 (Drupal risk 21 of 25)

Drupal's advisory SA-CONTRIB-2026-254 of 2026-10-28 says Commerce Core "doesn't sufficiently protect certain routes and entity fields, leading to an access bypass that may financially impact the vendor" and that the flaw is being actively exploited in the wild (Drupal Security Team, 2026-10-28); The Hacker News carries the same wording (The Hacker News, 2026-10-30). The Drupal security team scores it 21 of 25, which SecurityWeek reads as exploitable without authentication whatever the module's configuration, and Drupal's statistics put the module on more than 42,000 sites (SecurityWeek, 2026-10-30). The affected releases are Commerce Core 3.0.0 up to but not including 3.3.13 and earlier releases before 8.x-2.41 (SecurityWeek, 2026-10-30). Drupal has not said how the bug is exploited, by whom, how many sites were targeted or whether it was exploited before the fix (SecurityWeek, 2026-10-30); NCSC Switzerland's advisory of 2026-10-30 describes the impact as unauthenticated manipulation of order-related data with financial loss for the shop operator (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-30).

Exposure
Any Drupal site running Commerce Core below 3.3.13 on 3.x or below 8.x-2.41 on earlier releases, including shops built on the module's decoupled APIs rather than its own cart and checkout (The Hacker News, 2026-10-30); a public body that sells goods, permits or fees through such a site is in scope. The same day's batch holds 38 further Drupal advisories for 21 contributed projects, nearly a dozen rated critical, among them code execution, account takeover and Commerce orders marked as paid through Stripe without payment (SecurityWeek, 2026-10-30).
Detection
Drupal's own guidance is an order audit for inconsistencies (SecurityWeek, 2026-10-30); checking each order's state, totals and payment status against the payment provider's records is the obvious test, an inference since no source names a method. The sources name no routes, parameters or request patterns; the web-server access log of the shop's API and checkout routes is the other record to review, an inference since nothing describes the requests.
Defender takeaway
Update Commerce Core to 3.3.13 or 8.x-2.41 now and audit orders; the flaw needs no login and the upgrade is the only mitigation the sources name. Check the other contributed modules the site runs against the advisories of 2026-10-28.

Update31 Oct 2026 03:39 UTCrun 2026-10-31T0256Z-intelheadlinesummaryimmediate_actionsourcesevidenceactionsbody

Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis of CVE-2026-102764 on 2026-10-30 and says a Metasploit module now implements the unauthenticated file-write to code-execution chain; its successful request is an extensionless URL that rules matching only .php requests miss.

Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis on 2026-10-30 and says a Metasploit module now implements the chain, with PHP and Unix Command targets (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). An anonymous customer session, started through the public customer connection, sends a message whose source address carries a reserved local router ID; the appliance's customer worker accepts that address as proof that the request came from a local component, which exposes an internal file-transfer service with its native filesystem provider. Rapid7 used it to write a PHP file into the site's public directory and ran it as the site's operating-system user (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). The successful request was an extensionless URL, because the web server answers a direct .php request with 404 and maps an extensionless URL to the existing file, so detection that only searches for requests ending in .php would miss it; the appliance's thin-scc logs record file-transfer stream creation and rejected requests (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). Rapid7 tested Remote Support 24.1.2 and says other affected releases and fixed builds have not been established (Rapid7, 2026-10-30); BeyondTrust's advisory remains the reference for affected and fixed versions (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15).

The two earlier fires' attempts excluded 92 standard records from the slices; the breaches pool was small enough that S4 took its seven oldest-cursor records without the exclusion (bitdefender-threat-debrief, piyolog, ransom-isac, venarix, bleepingcomputer, cnil-fr, cyberinsider), so some were swept again.
  • Completeness follow-up: S1 dropped Progress WS_FTP Server and Veeam Management Pack on the strength of BSI's 'high' rating while CSIRT Italia counted 6 critical flaws including an authentication bypass, so one scoped follow-up (FU1, one continuation) read the vendor CNA records. WS_FTP clears PD-11(b) on its own mechanics: an unauthenticated network path to administrative credentials (CVSS 10.0) on a file-transfer server used with external partners, in a product whose 2023 flaw is in KEV with known ransomware use; no exploitation found, so it ships as notable with its fixed builds (2024.0.7, 2025.0.4). Progress's own bulletin is a script-rendered page no transport could read, so the entry's sourcing note says so.
  • borderline-drop: Veeam Management Pack for Microsoft System Center 9.x (KB 4961 of 2026-10-29), one unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2023-22793, CVSS 4.0 9.3, on servers running the Virtualization Extensions service) and two authenticated flaws; no exploitation, an internal management-plane add-in for System Center Operations Manager, and the fix is a move to 13.1.0.334 because 9.x gets no patch. Reopen on an exploitation report.
  • Source repairs from the health sweep: ec-digital-strategy-newsroom now reads through its RSS feed (general-news scope), sygnia joined the handled transport-blocked set, bfv-verfassungsschutz-de is checked through its feed recipe, and socprime is demoted on the content axis (its 20 newest feed items are product how-tos); ncsc-nl-php2shell-tracker and wordpress-org-news were promoted by the digest's promotion list; one new candidate, phorion.
  • Mid-run stop-hook nudges to commit were noted and ignored: the run commits atomically in Phase 6.
  • Spawn message error: the FU1 follow-up was told the time was about 04:40Z when it was about 03:55Z; its in-window anchor (2026-10-30T00:56Z) was stated explicitly and unaffected.
  • Single-source: Teams-to-AD CS (Microsoft Threat Intelligence is first-hand on both intrusions), Broadcom endpoint-security servers (Broadcom is the disclosing party; the SEPM fix builds rest on NCSC-NL's tracker and are marked unverified), and the Cisco, Trend Micro and QNAP revisions (vendor advisories for their own products). Each carries the matching sourcing_note.
  • Reduced confidence: Linux kernel CVE-2026-98432 carries confidence: medium because severity ratings disagree (9.8, 8.1, Critical for RHEL, 5.9 as BleepingComputer reported) and the exploit claim is Anthropic's alone; Broadcom SEPM fix builds as above. The drupal.org advisory answers a client challenge to extract, so its wording was read with WebFetch and the two quotes cited from it are not machine-checkable.
  • Dates: the Phorion post is dated 2026-10-30 with a 2026-10-31 update widening the version guidance from 2.1.313 to 2.1.312 and 2.1.313; Cursor's notice, Microsoft's analysis and Sophos agree. Broadcom's knowledge article 459982 shows a placeholder date (2026-01-01) in the extracted text; its structured data gives the publication date 2026-10-22, which the entry cites.
  • Contradiction: the Cursor extension entry. NCSC Switzerland's post 13121 places the backdoored extension on Open VSX and says Anthropic pulled npm and VS Code versions of 2.1.313; Microsoft says the packages were never published to the Visual Studio Marketplace or npm, and Cursor and Phorion name the Cursor marketplace only. The entry follows Microsoft, Cursor and Phorion and states the difference in its Exposure paragraph and sourcing note.
  • Contradiction held, not resolved: the Berlin Landesnetz entry records BSI's own confirmation that TerminalFix was the vector, while rbb24 writes that BSI did not confirm that pattern to it; no record was written (see the borderline-drop for that item).
  • borderline-drop: Pentagon commissary freezer failures (update-of the Danfoss refrigeration entry); attribution rests on two anonymous-source reports (Reuters via four officials, Nextgov via two people), no vector is stated, the lesson of the entry is unchanged, and the entry's analysis (1,291 words) is already far past the length bound, so a rewrite would be needed to carry it.
  • borderline-drop: Request Tracker 6.0.4 and 5.0.11, RTIR (30 CVEs), stored XSS from unauthenticated email and an authenticated code-execution bypass, no exploitation, and no source shows Swiss public-sector use; patch-cycle.
  • borderline-drop: Dell PowerProtect Data Domain DSA-2026-416, first published 2026-10-01 and last revised 2026-10-19, only NCSC-NL's relay of 2026-10-30 falls in the window; internal-facing backup appliance, no exploitation reported.
  • borderline-drop: Canonical LXD CVE-2026-112816 (CVSS 4.0 10.0, mTLS validation), niche stack, no exploitation, fixed 2026-10-29; patch-cycle.
  • borderline-drop: Siemens SSA-166980 revision 1.2; the revision predates the window and the energy products named have mostly no fix by design of the wave; the PHP2Shell OT entry already carries Siemens.
  • borderline-drop: GitLab 19.5.3 and the other 2026-10-29 patch releases removing the eight eMudhra intermediates (CVE-2026-111943), patch-cycle, no exploitation; the eMudhra entry's action already covers updating CA bundles and Go.
  • borderline-drop: Linux kernel PwnEscape CVE-2026-99999 (S1 bundled it with CVE-2026-98432), guest-to-host flaw, fixed since 2026-10-15, local vector; the expectation of exploits within weeks is the discoverer's, not an observation. It would be a separate entry if exploitation or a hypervisor exposure statement appears.
  • borderline-drop: Android 'SMS of Death' CVE-2026-58882, zero-click DoS on telephony, public PoC, fixed in the October bulletin; patch-cycle, status rests on heise alone.
  • borderline-drop: ReliaQuest victim-matched residential proxies in vishing-led SaaS intrusions, single vendor, the vishing pattern is covered by the Talos IR, Huntress and new Microsoft entries.
  • borderline-drop: TeamViewer TV-2026-1011 (CVE-2026-111585, viewer-side code execution), no exploitation, bulletin of 2026-10-28 outside the window; patch-cycle.
  • borderline-drop: CrowdStrike 2026 Legal Threat Landscape Report (annual-report candidate), legal sector outside the constituency, report gated; the transferable content (IT-impersonation vishing into remote tools) is covered.
  • borderline-drop: Binance (about USD 6.36 billion, largest crypto theft on record; S3 and S4 returned it), clears breach limb (a) on scale only; no Swiss public-sector nexus, the stated vector (a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop) is covered ground, so an entry would be awareness only. Reopen if a post-mortem names a transferable technique.
  • borderline-drop: Berlin Landesnetz detection gap (rbb24, attack-detection licences covering 5 percent of devices); the rbb24 primary is 10 days old and only a blog relay is in the window; an organisational lesson that changes no detection decision.
  • borderline-drop: RMS Cloud and feratel Deskline booking-platform breaches, no Swiss customer named at either vendor; same WhatsApp booking-fraud pattern as the covered Camping.Care entry.
  • borderline-drop: SIHF and Swiss Basketball member-portal incidents, private associations; the 2026-10-30 fire dropped SIHF for the same reason, and the basketball claim rests on FrenchBreaches alone.
  • borderline-drop: Fehmarnbelt contractor FLC, Leipzig University and Charité, Ruag MRO law-firm investigation, FortiBleed 2.0 (Hudson Rock), no Swiss entity or no vector or actor (incident floor), the Ruag item is insider fraud without an intrusion, and the FortiBleed data is dated February with no new vector.
  • borderline-drop: S2's policy and enforcement candidates (Federal Council e-evidence transitional rule, DVS Microsoft 365 exit study, BACS WhatsApp fake-vote update, Qilin arrest, INTERPOL Serengeti III); no change to what the constituency's defenders are obliged or advised to do, or outside the window. Canton Bern's ICSG enters into force 2026-11-01 and is already in the store.
  • S3 left three out-of-window leads for the audit to weigh, none fetched as a primary: Microsoft Authenticator CVE-2026-80097 (2026-10-28), EDK II PXE flaw CVE-2026-97631 (seen only in a search summary), and the 2026-10-29 research posts from Talos (NIK C2), Securelist (NetamLoader) and Group-IB (MadApe).
  • Coverage gaps: ivanti advisory hub (login shell on every transport; per-CVE fixed builds unconfirmed); connectwise-trust-center (403, WebSearch only); ox-security (article bodies 403); resecurity, onapsis, openjdk-vulnerability-advisories, zimbra-security-advisories (listings unreadable or empty); broadcom advisories 39411 and 39421 (login-gated). Recipe findings are recorded in the sources_changed notes: schneier, blick-ch, qnap, synology, siemens, the NCSC-NL tracker change log.
  • Verification: iteration 3 returned NEEDS_FIXES with 2 truth and 0 editorial findings (none F1 or F4) on full coverage (238 of 238 claims); all five of its findings were fixed in the entries and the run published on the low-residual early exit without a fourth pass, so the two truth fixes are unconfirmed by a later cold read (residual count 2).

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-30
item.description:
• CISA lists WordPress core's upgrade-window RCE race as exploited; block wp-content/upgrade before installing 7.1.4. WordPress 7.1.4 of 2026-10-28 fixes a weakness in the core upgrade process that lets an unauthenticated attacker reach the staged installer and run code on the server during a full-package core update, in versions 4.7 to 7.1.3, with backports for every branch down to 4.7. CISA added CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-03; Wordfence reports more than 18,500 probing requests in the first 21 hours, while Patchstack calls the race hard to win and says it needs a web-reachable staging directory. The discoverer says the update that installs the fix still unpacks with the old code, so the staging directory must be blocked before updating. →
  • Cisco ASA and FTD SSL VPN reload flaw is exploited and on CISA KEV; fixes in every branch, no workaround. Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-28 fixes CVE-2026-76418, a logic error in the remote access SSL VPN of Secure Firewall ASA and Secure FTD that lets an unauthenticated attacker reload the device with a crafted connection request when a tunnel group uses secondary authentication, and says Cisco's PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in October 2026; CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-29. Cisco names no actor, offers no workaround and lists first fixed releases for every ASA and FTD branch. →
  • Lumen: Volt Typhoon's Silent Train relay chains fronted zero-days against SD-WAN, N-central and KACE. Lumen's Black Lotus Labs reports that Volt Typhoon ran exploitation, credential access and exfiltration through Silent Train, rotating chains of compromised SOHO, IoT and enterprise devices that it rebuilt for each operation, and that its monitoring uncovered one likely and four confirmed zero-day campaigns against endpoint and network management platforms and SD-WAN orchestrators, among them Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, N-able N-central and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator. The reported victims are US-centred and the report names no Swiss or European victim. →

TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01CISA lists WordPress core's upgrade-window RCE race as exploited; block wp-content/upgrade before installing 7.1.4. WordPress 7.1.4 of 2026-10-28 fixes a weakness in the core upgrade process that lets an unauthenticated attacker reach the staged installer and run code on the server during a full-package core update, in versions 4.7 to 7.1.3, with backports for every branch down to 4.7. CISA added CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-03; Wordfence reports more than 18,500 probing requests in the first 21 hours, while Patchstack calls the race hard to win and says it needs a web-reachable staging directory. The discoverer says the update that installs the fix still unpacks with the old code, so the staging directory must be blocked before updating. →
  2. 02Cisco ASA and FTD SSL VPN reload flaw is exploited and on CISA KEV; fixes in every branch, no workaround. Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-28 fixes CVE-2026-76418, a logic error in the remote access SSL VPN of Secure Firewall ASA and Secure FTD that lets an unauthenticated attacker reload the device with a crafted connection request when a tunnel group uses secondary authentication, and says Cisco's PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in October 2026; CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-29. Cisco names no actor, offers no workaround and lists first fixed releases for every ASA and FTD branch. →
  3. 03Lumen: Volt Typhoon's Silent Train relay chains fronted zero-days against SD-WAN, N-central and KACE. Lumen's Black Lotus Labs reports that Volt Typhoon ran exploitation, credential access and exfiltration through Silent Train, rotating chains of compromised SOHO, IoT and enterprise devices that it rebuilt for each operation, and that its monitoring uncovered one likely and four confirmed zero-day campaigns against endpoint and network management platforms and SD-WAN orchestrators, among them Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, N-able N-central and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator. The reported victims are US-centred and the report names no Swiss or European victim. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 2Trending vulnerabilities 2Research, reports & policy 2Updates to prior coverage 5Action items 6

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures2 items

NOTABLENATOB3

VAPOR PANDA: CrowdStrike reports a China-nexus actor running the ARTEX agent framework against more than 200 organisations from 17 October, among them foreign ministries in Europe and a Greek government entity, and deploying the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor

CrowdStrike OverWatch reports that from 2026-10-17 a single ARTEX controller linked to VAPOR PANDA infrastructure directed exploitation against entities in at least 14 countries over 11 days, and that the campaign reached more than 200 organisations, including foreign ministries in Europe (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). One engagement focused on a single European country, its foreign ministry, presidency, prime minister's office and defence, justice, finance and intelligence entities, and another targeted 19 US organisations in pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, defence, nuclear and finance (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). CrowdStrike confirmed post-exploitation at nine organisations and password spraying and credential scanning against at least 12 more, among them government entities in Europe (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). CrowdStrike states that the campaign is separate from the Storm-0940 ARTEX activity Microsoft reported and is VAPOR PANDA's first observed use of AI-driven tooling (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29).

The framework ran mainly on the DeepSeek model, with a human operator steering the agents at decision points while they pursued web, cloud, container, Active Directory, mail and VPN paths in parallel (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). In transcripts at a US pharmaceutical company the agent chained an unsigned SAML assertion with an XML external entity flaw to query the cloud instance metadata service and obtain a role that could issue administration commands to thousands of instances; at a second it deployed web shells, abused an unauthenticated orchestration service for root in a container environment, read LAPS passwords and abused resource-based constrained delegation (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). Against a Greek government entity the operator supplied a 2022 directory export from the mail server whose authentication keys had likely not been rotated; the agent forged an administrator token, read mailboxes and used VPN configurations from a user's sent mail, with a VPN client key the operator described as coming from a May 2024 email leak, to reach the internal network (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). The operator also told the agents to find domain Windows hosts without the CrowdStrike Falcon sensor (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). At a Middle East interior ministry and a Latin American foreign ministry the actor loaded the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor through a legitimate GameHook binary renamed svchost.exe that loads a malicious DLL (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). No Swiss target is named.

Exposure
Government, mail, identity and VPN estates where a directory export or backup holding authentication keys has never been rotated, SAML service providers that accept unsigned assertions, and cloud instances that still allow instance metadata service version 1; CrowdStrike names foreign ministries and government entities in Europe among the targets (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29).
Detection
Telemetry classes are authentication logs (password spraying and credential scanning against many accounts, an administrator token minted outside the identity provider, VPN logins that use a configuration or key from an old mailbox or leak), cloud control-plane audit (administration commands issued to many instances through the cloud systems manager, instance metadata queries from an application), process lineage (a legitimate GameHook binary renamed svchost.exe loading a malicious DLL) and endpoint inventory queries for hosts without the security agent; CrowdStrike lists ARTEX-named command-line parameters, cloud roles and a directory under ProgramData as hunt markers (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29).
Defender takeaway
Rotate keys held in old directory exports and backups, require signed SAML assertions and IMDSv2, and hunt authentication and cloud audit logs for the parallel, many-target pattern an operator-steered agent produces; CrowdStrike expects China-nexus actors to keep adopting agent frameworks (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29).

Builds on: 2026-10-22/artex-storm-0940-agentic-llm-pentest-spraying-oauth-abuse · 2026-10-26/jpcert-nict-app-to-backend-api-attacks-ai-scanning-japan

threat30 Oct 03:48Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: CrowdStrike
NOTABLENATOB2

Silent Train: Lumen's Black Lotus Labs describes the rotating relay network Volt Typhoon used for one likely and four confirmed zero-day campaigns against management and control-plane platforms (Quest KACE, Versa Director, N-able N-central, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator)

Lumen's Black Lotus Labs reports that Volt Typhoon used a covert framework it calls Silent Train, first seen in late 2023, for the phases that need protection: exploitation, credential access, data exfiltration and continued access to victims (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). A session starts from a virtual private server outside the US, passes through compromised non-US SOHO and IoT devices and leaves through a compromised US device before the victim; more than 27 device classes were enrolled, from TP-Link routers and Netgear Orbi devices to Fortinet appliances and CyberPanel servers, and the enterprise platforms stayed in chains for one to three months as final hops (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). The operators exploit exposed web interfaces on the relay devices and deploy only what chained SSH needs, namely temporary SSH services, keys, configuration files and living-off-the-land utilities, with reverse tunnels over open-source proxies in later variants; sessions averaged about four hours, and at the end the operators removed all artifacts and dismantled the chain (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28).

Lumen says its monitoring helped identify one likely and four confirmed zero-day campaigns against endpoint and network management platforms and SD-WAN orchestrators: Quest KACE, where the activity looked like an undisclosed flaw, affected more than 30 victims and fell after Quest's October 2025 updates (a moderate-confidence assessment); Versa Director in 2024; the N-able N-central flaws CVE-2025-8875 and CVE-2025-8876; Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN through CVE-2026-20127, exploited by late 2025 and after Cisco's February 2026 disclosure; and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator through the zero-day later designated CVE-2026-16812 (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). Post-incident analysis found in-memory webshells, credential harvesting and abuse of native platform features such as endpoint control and remote file transfers, and in several cases erased or altered logs (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). The victims it names are US government, telecommunications, defence-industrial, managed-service and critical-infrastructure organisations, concentrated in Hawaii, California and Texas, and it names no European or Swiss victim (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). The Hacker News carries the same findings from a report Lumen shared with it (The Hacker News, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
Internet-reachable management and control-plane platforms (endpoint management, SD-WAN controllers and orchestrators, out-of-band administration), and edge devices with exposed web interfaces, which can be enrolled as relay hops without any data of the owner being the target.
Detection
Telemetry classes are administrative logins, API calls, remote file transfers and configuration changes on management platforms outside normal administration hours or workflow, in-memory web shells that leave no file on disk, and, on edge devices, temporary SSH services, unfamiliar keys and outbound reverse tunnels to unfamiliar upstream hosts (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28).
Defender takeaway
Restrict the administrative interfaces of management and control-plane platforms to a VPN, jump host or management network and prioritise their patching, as Lumen advises, and treat an edge device that shows temporary SSH services or reverse tunnels as a possible relay in someone else's intrusion chain.

Builds on: 2026-10-29/keydrift-uat-11473-cisco-sd-wan-controllers-cve-2026-20127 · 2026-07-28/cve-2026-16812-arista-velocloud-orchestrator-exploited · 2026-10-23/cve-2026-114625-arista-velocloud-orchestrator-sqli-exploited · 2026-10-29/php2shell-trend-micro-apex-quest-kace-netapp-ontap

threat30 Oct 03:50Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Lumen Black Lotus Labs · The Hacker News

02Trending vulnerabilities2 items

HIGHCVE-2026-119977exploitedupdatedNATOA2

WordPress core 4.7 to 7.1.3: an unauthenticated race in the core update process can lead to remote code execution, fixed in 7.1.4 and backported to every supported branch, listed by CISA as exploited; Wordfence assigned CVE-2026-119977

WordPress 7.1.4, released on 2026-10-28, fixes a weakness in the upgrade process that can lead to remote code execution during the upgrade window, and backports follow for every branch that receives security fixes, currently through 4.7 (WordPress.org, 2026-10-28). During a core update with a complete package, the new files are unpacked into a predictable directory under wp-content/upgrade; the temporary copy includes the installer, and an unauthenticated attacker who requests it at the right moment can interact with the staged copy and reach PHP code execution (Wordfence, 2026-10-29). Wordfence scores it CVSS 8.1 for versions 4.7 through 7.1.3 and states that the attack complexity is high, because the attacker needs web access to the staging tree and must win a race that lasted only seconds in its lab (Wordfence, 2026-10-29). Patchstack reads the same flaw as needing wp-content/upgrade/ to be reachable over the web and would not call it practical to exploit (Patchstack, 2026-10-28).

Wordfence reports that its new firewall rule matched within nine minutes of deployment and that it recorded more than 18,500 requests for staged setup-config.php installer paths in the first 21 hours (Wordfence, 2026-10-29). CISA lists the flaw as exploited, and no source names a victim or describes a successful compromise (CISA, 2026-11-03). The fix randomises the staging directory, adds an index guard and prevents unsafe promotion of staged configuration data (Wordfence, 2026-10-29).

Exposure
Any WordPress site on 4.7 to 7.1.3 with wp-content/upgrade/ reachable from the internet while a core update runs; the discoverer says the deciding factor is whether the updater already installed on the site has been fixed, so the update to 7.1.4 is exposed too, automatic updates included, although a partial package exposes the installer only if it contains the installer files (The Hacker News, 2026-11-06); on 5.9 or later the staging folder name can be predicted, on 4.4 to 5.8 a random suffix hides it unless the site leaks it, and 4.6 and earlier, which Picus counts as affected back to 2.7, get no fix (Picus Security, 2026-11-05). The fixed releases are 7.1.4 and the backport of each branch (7.0.8, 6.9.11 and so on down to 4.7.39) (Wordfence, 2026-10-29).
Detection
In web server access logs, requests under wp-content/upgrade/ and for setup-config.php inside a staging directory, repeated from one source against a few sites as Wordfence saw (Wordfence, 2026-10-29); between updates the directory holds only an index.php (Patchstack, 2026-10-28). Where an unpatched site updated with the directory reachable, check that wp-config.php, which the attack overwrites, still names your database (Picus Security, 2026-11-05) and look for administrator accounts, plugins and PHP files under wp-content/upgrade/ that nobody created (The Hacker News, 2026-11-06).

Triage: a request to a staging path outside an update window finds only an index.php and is probing, not compromise; a successful response from the staged installer during an update is the event that matters.

Defender takeaway
Deny web access to wp-content/upgrade/ at the web server and confirm it answers 403 before the update runs, then confirm that the update completed on every site instead of assuming it, because a firewall that WordPress itself loads cannot block the request: the staged copy loads from its own files (Patchstack, 2026-10-28); Wordfence's blocking rule helps only where its firewall is set up to run before direct PHP requests reach their file (Wordfence, 2026-10-29).
Correction01 Nov 2026 13:52 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditbodycvessourcessourcing_notesummarytitle

The flaw now has an identifier: Wordfence tracks it as CVE-2026-119977, a time-of-check time-of-use race condition scored CVSS 3.1 8.1 (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N), affecting WordPress 4.7.0 to 7.1.3 with the same fixed releases as above (Wordfence Intelligence, 2026-10-31). The statement that no source assigns a CVE identifier is withdrawn; scanners and asset inventories can now match the flaw by that ID.

Update04 Nov 2026 03:25 UTCrun 2026-11-04T0256Z-intelcvesprioritytagsheadlinesummarytitlesourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

CISA added CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-03 on evidence of active exploitation (CISA, 2026-11-03), and the Canadian Cyber Centre's advisory of the same day relays the listing for WordPress Core before 7.1.4 (Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, 2026-11-03). The listing names no victim, attacker behaviour or exploitation method, so Wordfence's probing telemetry above remains the only described activity and Patchstack's high-complexity rating still stands. A site that ran a full-package core update on 4.7 to 7.1.3 while wp-content/upgrade/ was reachable needs the compromise check in the Detection line, not only the update.

Update07 Nov 2026 03:51 UTCrun 2026-11-07T0256Z-intelheadlinesummaryactionssourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

Umut Bayram of Picus Security, who found the flaw, shows that the update which installs the fix still unpacks its files with the site's old, unpatched code (Picus Security, 2026-11-05; The Hacker News, 2026-11-06). Picus says the new code's skip of wp-config.php already works in that first update but the randomised folder name does not, so the temporary installer sits at a predictable path on sites running 5.9 or later and, on 4.4 to 5.8, behind a random suffix that hides it unless the site leaks the path; an attacker who reaches it can no longer replace the live configuration but can still set up the temporary copy, log in to it, run PHP and from there read or write files in the live directory (Picus Security, 2026-11-05). Bayram told The Hacker News the deciding factor "isn’t partial versus complete. It’s whether the updater already installed on the site has been fixed", and that a partial package exposes the installer only if it contains the installer files; The Hacker News found WordPress.org offering an in-branch move such as 7.1.3 to 7.1.4 as a partial package, automatic updates included, so whether such an update is exposed depends on what that package contains, and only once 7.1.4 or the branch fix is installed do later updates use a random folder (The Hacker News, 2026-11-06). WordPress 4.6 and earlier get no fix (The Hacker News, 2026-11-06).

The order matters: Picus advises denying web access to wp-content/upgrade/ in the web server configuration first, confirming that the path answers 403, and only then updating; this does not break updates, because WordPress reaches the folder through the filesystem (Picus Security, 2026-11-05). An .htaccess file placed inside the folder does not work, because the old updater deletes the folder's contents before unpacking, and WP-CLI's wp core update is no substitute because it uses the same updater and folder (Picus Security, 2026-11-05). For sites that stayed on an affected version, Wordfence suggests looking for unexpected requests to PHP files under wp-content/upgrade, administrator accounts no one recognises, plugins no one installed and PHP files in wp-content/upgrade that no one put there (The Hacker News, 2026-11-06).

Code that its authors describe as an exploit has appeared in public GitHub repositories since earlier this week, and whether it works has not been established; WordPress's own advisory rates the flaw low, against Wordfence's CVSS 8.1 and CISA's listing as exploited (The Hacker News, 2026-11-06). None of these sources reports a compromise through the update that installs the fix; CISA's listing and Wordfence's probing telemetry above are unchanged.

Improvement08 Nov 2026 14:08 UTCrun 2026-11-08T1309Z-auditbody

The configuration check in the Detection line follows from the mechanism Picus describes: an attacker creates a malicious wp-config.php inside the temporary update directory and has the updater copy it over the live configuration, which can redirect the site to an attacker-controlled empty database (Picus Security, 2026-11-05).

vulnerability30 Oct 03:45Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: WordPress.org · Wordfence · Patchstack · Wordfence Intelligence (CVE-2026-119977) · CISA · Canadian Centre for Cyber Security · Picus Security · The Hacker News
